447: Built around Masters of the Maelstrom, Chosen, Defilers, Huron Blackheart, Abaddon the Despoiler, Chaos Terminator Squads, and waves of Cultist Mobs, this list layers the Cabal of Chaos's Dark Pact buffs onto Psyker shooting and Daemon Prince combat output while the Fellhammer Siege-Host's wound-roll penalty makes the whole army punishingly durable against overstrength weapons. The game plan is to drown the board in Cultist chaff screens, grind objectives through sheer body count, and let Abaddon and Chosen punch through whatever survives — Dark Pacts amplifying both ranged and melee kill chains throughout. It punishes elite low-volume armies that rely on high-Strength guns to crack targets efficiently, since Fellhammer directly degrades those wound rolls. It cracks open against high-AP, high-volume fire that ignores the wound-roll reduction by simply matching or falling under target Toughness, and coordinated alpha strikes that collapse the cultist screen before the midfield brawlers can engage.
448: Built around Defilers, Venomcrawlers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Warpsmiths supported by Cultist Mob screens, this is a Daemon Vehicle-heavy warpack running Cabal of Chaos with a majority also taking Soulforged Warpack — stacking Dark Pact payoffs across mechanised killers that hit harder when their contracts are invoked. The win condition is grinding the midboard with resilient Daemon Vehicles that, under Soulforged Warpack's Dark Pact, gain +1 to wound on ranged attacks and +2 Attacks in melee simultaneously, while Vashtorr and Warpsmiths keep those engines repaired and fighting. It brutally punishes armour-heavy lists, threatening vehicles and monsters from range and then brawling them down in melee with overloaded attack profiles. Armies that can screen out the midboard engagement, suppress Dark Pacts through repeated Leadership pressure, or alpha-strike the Daemon Vehicles before they invoke can crack the engine before it hits full output.
450: Built around Wyches, Incubi, Lady Malys, Drazhar, Lelith Hesperax, and Succubi packed into Venoms and Raiders, this is a mass-transport assault list running Skysplinter Assault and Exhibition of Slaughter together. The engine is disembark-and-delete: units pile out of skimmers to hit with Ignores Cover ranged fire and Lance melee, while Exhibition of Slaughter grants Wych Cult melee attacks Lethal Hits against non-Monster, non-Vehicle targets, letting the horde of Wyches and Succubi butcher infantry hordes on contact. It punishes objective-camping infantry lists brutally — the sheer volume of Lethal Hits attacks combined with Lance on disembark turns any close engagement into a wipeout. Opponents who can strip transports early strand the payload mid-board, and anything with enough anti-tank output to crack Venoms at range leaves the glass-hammer infantry exposed before they ever disembark.
466: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Tormentors, Lord Exultants, Defilers, Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Lucius the Eternal, and Chaos Rhinos, this is a Coterie of the Conceited transport-infantry swarm that floods midfield with mobile, hard-hitting units across every threat bracket. The win engine is the Pact point pledge mechanic — you commit to a kill count each round and earn Pact points when you hit that number, so the list is built to reliably trade up by delivering multiple infantry units into contact simultaneously via Rhinos while Defilers and Daemon Princes apply mobile anti-armour pressure. It punishes slower, spread-thin gunlines that struggle to answer overlapping threat vectors before the pledge thresholds snowball Pact point generation. However, elite alpha-strike armies that can delete key transports and infantry before contact force failed pledges, collapsing the economy that makes the list function.
473: Built around Paladin Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, Grand Master Voldus, Brotherhood Chaplains, and supporting Strike and Interceptor Squads, this list runs the Argent Assault detachment to ensure Paladins wound up even when punching into high-Toughness targets. The win condition is layered melee pressure across multiple fronts — Paladins grind through elite infantry and monsters while Terminators, frequently supplemented by Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back and fight/shoot ability, contest and reclaim objectives without surrendering board presence after a bad combat. It punishes slow, durable armies that rely on Toughness to survive melee, since the core detachment strips that defensive buffer from Paladins entirely, and the mobile toolkit of Interceptors keeps the pressure spread wide. However, high-volume shooting lists that can strip Paladins before they engage, or armies that deny the melee phase through layered screens, crack this build open by neutering the wound-roll engine before it fires.
481: Built around the Knight Castellan, this list uses the Dominus Foebreakers detachment to squeeze extra hit rolls out of its heaviest hitters whenever enemies shelter in terrain — punishing the cover-hugging play that typically counters big Knights. The win condition is straightforward anti-armour overload: the Castellan's massed high-strength output dictates the engagement while Armiger screens and supporting Knights create threat across the entire board. It punishes elite vehicle lists that rely on terrain for protection, turning cover into a liability rather than a defence through the detachment's hit-roll bonus. Horde infantry and cheap objective-flooding armies can be harder to crack efficiently, and the Castellan's relatively low model count leaves this list vulnerable to being out-activated and out-scored on secondary objectives.
480: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Armiger Helverins, a Knight Crusader, and a Knight Castellan, this list floods the table with medium and large walkers across every threat range. The plan is to apply relentless anti-armour pressure from multiple angles simultaneously — Helverins suppress at range while Warglaives chase down vehicles and monsters in melee, forcing opponents to split resources and concede priority targets. It punishes armour-heavy lists badly, stacking mobile anti-armour output that most vehicle-dense builds simply cannot absorb across multiple turns. Where it struggles is against elite infantry and screens: the list lacks the concentrated anti-horde volume to efficiently clear bodies off objectives, leaving it vulnerable to anything that can park cheap wounds in the way and deny scoring.
430: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard, Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, and Hekaton Land Fortresses, supported by fast-moving Hernkyn Pioneers, Yaegirs, and Kapricus Carriers, this is a mid-board brawler that floods every quarter with armoured infantry and hard-hitting fire support. The Hearthguard Covenant detachment's wound-reroll-on-1 rule within 9" rewards aggressive positioning, so the plan is to push Hearthguard and a Kâhl deep into the midfield and grind opponents apart in close range while Thunderkyn and Steeljacks lay down sustained heavy fire from slightly further back. It punishes elite-infantry and light-vehicle lists particularly hard — massed re-rolled wound rolls at short range shred anything without a serious damage-reduction stack. Swarm lists or opponents who can force combat across a wide frontage will stretch the brick thin, and anything that keeps the Hearthguard outside 9" strips the core re-roll engine entirely.
482: Built around Armiger Warglaives, Cerastus Knight Lancers, Knight Castellans, Knight Crusaders, and Armiger Helverins, this is a full-roster Knights army running Freeblade Company — every model benefits from Feel No Pain 6+ and ticks back 1 wound per Command phase, making the entire force meaningfully harder to grind down. The win condition is mobile anti-armour dominance: Lancers crack heavy targets in melee while Castellans and Crusaders saturate the board with high-volume firepower, with Hunter's Eye and Mysterious Guardian enhancing key pieces to punish anything with a large wound pool. It excels against elite and vehicle-heavy lists that struggle to efficiently trade into multiple hardened big models before the passive regeneration compounds. Swarm armies and high-volume mortal-wound output crack it open by overwhelming the FNP rolls faster than the regen can compensate, and the limited model count makes each individual loss disproportionately painful on objectives.
456: Built around Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancers, Canoptek Doomstalkers, Canoptek Reanimators, and the Void Dragon, this Canoptek Court list feels like a living machine swarm — durable, self-repairing, and everywhere at once. The win condition is map control through the Power Matrix: dominate No Man's Land's objectives to extend your buff zone beyond your deployment zone, then let Doomstalkers and the Void Dragon grind down whatever sits on those markers while Technomancers keep the swarm cycling back. It punishes slow, durable gunlines that can't quickly clear multiple resilient threats across the board, overwhelming their repair capacity through layered, stacking lethality. It struggles against fast aggressive lists that can contest objectives before the Power Matrix activates, or high-volume anti-infantry shooting that kills Wraiths faster than Reanimators and Technomancers can restore them.
486: Built around nearly five squads of Boyz supported by Painboyz, Warbosses, Bigbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, Wazdakka Gutsmek, and Weirdboyz, this is Green Tide in its purest form — a wall of green bodies running the table under the detachment's rule that grants Boyz units of 10 or more models a 5+ invulnerable save against every incoming attack. The plan is to flood the midboard with virtually unkillable blobs, grind through opposing units in melee, and outscore on attrition by making every kill more expensive than your opponent budgeted for. It punishes low-volume, high-damage lists that expect each shot to delete a unit — when those attacks hit a 10+ model squad with a 5+ invuln, the math collapses in your favor. Against high-volume shooting or templates that bypass that invulnerable save through sheer number of attacks, the wall eventually crumbles faster than your Painboyz can patch it.
487: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, multiple Beastbosses, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Kill Rigs, and Mozrog Skragbad, this is Da Big Hunt in action — a wall of Beast Snagga units crashing into midfield backed by heavy cavalry and lumbering war engines. The plan is to designate a high-value enemy unit as Prey each Command phase, then funnel charge re-rolls into your most dangerous Beast Snagga units to guarantee contact and grind opponents off objectives through sheer melee pressure. Kill Rigs and Squighog Boyz provide mobile anti-armour punch that punishes vehicle-heavy lists unwilling or unable to screen their assets. Armies that can deny melee engagement through strong shooting, deep strike denial, or fast objective repositioning expose the build's reliance on surviving long enough to charge.
468: Built around Vulkan He'stan, two blocks of Infernus Squads, Land Raider Redeemers, and Librarians supported by Adrax Agatone and Bladeguard Veterans, this is a Forgefather's Seekers gunline that turns short-range flame weapons into Assault, +1 Strength within 12" murder engines. The win condition is closing distance fast — Redeemers deliver Infernus Squads into the 12" sweet spot where Seeker's Companions activates alongside Vulkan's presence, then the Librarius Conclave layers Pyromancy or Divination on top to delete whatever they touch. It punishes horde armies and lightly-armoured infantry catastrophically, since massed Assault flamers with boosted Strength at close range strip bodies faster than most lists can screen. Spread-out, long-range armies that can avoid the 12" kill zone and apply anti-tank pressure on the Redeemers before they deliver their cargo crack this list open before the engine ever fires.
488: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Tankbustas, Flash Gitz, Big Mek Dakkarigas, and Wazdakka Gutsmek, all operating under Dread Mob with the More Dakka! strat layered on top, this is a horde gunline that floods the table with Gretchin screens while its shooting units churn out enormous volumes of fire. The engine is Dread Mob's D6 weapon-ability roll supercharging Mek and Walker units each phase, with More Dakka! granting Assault and Waaagh!-fuelled Sustained Hits 1 to infantry shooting, letting Lootas and Flash Gitz punish across movement phases while Tankbustas handle heavy armour. It brutalises armies that need to close distance to score, as Trukk-mounted units threaten the midboard while layered Gretchin screens deny easy objective pressure. It cracks open when opponents strip screens early with blast weapons or apply consistent anti-infantry volume that collapses the Gretchin buffer before the gunline can pay off its investment.
467: Built around Marneus Calgar, the Victrix Honour Guard, Repulsor Executioners, and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, this Blade of Ultramar list combines a heavily protected melee anchor with a rotating heavy gunline that cycles Combat Doctrines each Command phase — and Calgar's unique ability to re-select already-used Doctrines lets the list double back on its strongest phase when it matters most. The win condition is layering Calgar's Doctrine flexibility over concentrated ranged firepower from multiple Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, grinding opponents off objectives while the Honour Guard keep Calgar alive through trades. It punishes slower, durable armies — think multi-wound infantry blobs and vehicle-heavy lists — where sustained heavy fire across multiple turns compounds damage faster than the opponent can answer. It cracks against aggressive alpha-strike builds and elite melee armies that can bypass or overwhelm the Honour Guard screen before the gunline generates enough return fire to stabilise.
428: Built around Riptides, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinders, Crisis Starscythes, Broadsides, a Stormsurge, Piranhas, and the Twin Lance, this is a Mont'Ka list that turns the entire army into a rolling firebase from turn one — every ranged weapon gains [ASSAULT], letting heavy hitters move and shoot without penalty, while Guided units layer [LETHAL HITS] on top for devastating efficiency. The win condition is simple anti-armour attrition: flood the board with high-strength fire early, strip opposing heavy units before they can threaten back, and use Piranhas and Stealth Battlesuits to screen objectives and dictate positioning. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, overwhelming them with massed mobile shooting that generates lethal hits on virtually every guided salvo. It struggles against armies that can deep-strike or rush into close engagement quickly, collapsing the Guided synergy chain by forcing the T'au into melee or denying clean lines of sight in the early rounds when [ASSAULT] and [LETHAL HITS] are live.
483: Built around Norn Emissaries with Protean Purpose, Broodlord-led Genestealer blobs, Von Ryan's Leapers, Lictors, and Biovores providing backfield pressure, this is a hyper-mobile toolbox list that floods the board with fast, independent threat vectors. The win condition is overwhelming opponent decision-making — Genestealers and Leapers crash into midboard objectives early while Norn Emissaries and Tyrannofexes grind out kills to deny opponent scoring, with Biovores softening screens from safety. It punishes static gunlines that lack the volume of fire to address simultaneous threats from multiple angles, particularly lists that can't screen against deep infiltrators. However, it struggles against anything that can alpha-strike its fragile elite infantry before they engage, or that projects enough durable Objective Control to simply outscore the swarm's piecemeal pressure.
490: Built around Sekhetar Robots, Defilers, Forgefiends, Tzaangor Shamans, Exalted Sorcerers on Disc, Ahriman, and Daemon Princes with Wings, this is a psyker-infused mechanised gunline that turns its robots into Psychic-keyed melee threats while stacking Vehicles across the board. The Shamans and Sorcerers hang within 12" of the Robots to boost their WS, while Defilers and Forgefiends operate near Psykers to fish re-rolls on hit, wound, and damage through Warpforged Cabal, creating a layered kill chain that punishes both infantry screens and armoured targets simultaneously. It excels against lists that lack the volume or AP to strip Vehicles efficiently, since the Robot-Psyker synergy forces opponents to split priority between melee and shooting threats. Dense anti-armour lists that can kite outside the 12" aura bubble collapse the WS bonus and neuter the close-range engine before it engages.
489: Built around Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators led by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Daemon Princes of Tzeentch with Wings, Sekhetar Robots, and Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, the Hexwarp Thrallband floods the board with layered, durable infantry and fast flanking threats. The win condition is controlling objectives across No Man's Land and your deployment zone to unlock the Flow of Magic, then leveraging that sustained magical output and massed bodies to grind opponents off points while skimmer fire from Enlightened picks apart exposed screens. It punishes elite low-model armies hard, as massed layered lethality and sheer unit volume overwhelm armies that can't answer multiple durable threats simultaneously. It cracks open against hyper-mobile or alpha-strike lists that can deny objective control early, collapsing the Flow of Magic engine before it generates meaningful advantage.
427: Built around Crisis Battlesuits in every flavour — Sunforge, Starscythe, Fireknife — alongside Commander Farsight, multiple Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, The Twin Lance, Stealth Battlesuits, and Pathfinders, this is a wall-to-wall battlesuit army running Kauyon as its primary detachment. The plan is to survive early turns screening with Stealth Battlesuits and Vespid Stingwings while Pathfinders light up targets, then detonate in rounds three through five when Kauyon's Sustained Hits 1 and ignore-modifier buff turns the entire army into a precision kill machine. It punishes armour-heavy and multi-wound lists hard, with mobile anti-tank firepower that can reposition and delete key pieces across the mid-table. Armies that can alpha-strike the screening layer or deny Spotting chains before round three starve the engine of its payoff window entirely.
484: Built around Norn Assimilators, Norn Emissaries, Biovores, Pyrovores, Psychophage, and the Swarmlord, this list weaponizes the Assimilation Swarm detachment's Harvester regeneration engine — returning slain infantry models and healing wounded monsters every Command phase — to make its frontline effectively impossible to permanently clear. The win condition is attrition through presence: flood mid-table with regenerating bodies and resilient monstrous creatures that force opponents to kill the same units twice while Biovores chip objectives and Pyrovores punish anything that tries to dig into the blob. It brutally punishes low-volume, high-quality shooting lists that can't sustain the throughput needed to outpace the heal loop, especially against multi-wound monsters benefiting from Protean Purpose flexibility. It cracks open against high-AP, high-volume armies that can delete entire squads in a single phase before regeneration triggers, or elite close-combat forces that bypass the recursion by simply tabling units faster than they return.
518: Built around Nekrosor Ammentar, Lokhust Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Skorpekh Destroyers, Skorpekh Lords, a Lokhust Lord, and the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, this Skyshroud Spearhead list is a mobile Destroyer Cult swarm that floods the board with threat vectors from multiple angles. The win condition is a cascading kill chain: Cursed Legion's Strength buff activates the moment any Destroyer Cult unit deletes or half-strips an enemy unit, supercharging subsequent attacks in the same turn and letting the list snowball through a target-rich midfield. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot absorb multi-directional pressure simultaneously, as Ophydians arrive from underground, Lokhust Destroyers fire from range, and the C'tan anchors a durable midfield anchor. Armies that can screen out deep strike corridors, spread thin across objectives, and force the kill chain to stall on durable chaff will crack this list before the Strength escalation ever fires.
517: Built around paired Doomsday Arks, the Silent King, Canoptek Wraiths, Technomancer-supported Flayed Ones, and Ophydian Destroyers, this list plays a punishing objective-pressure game under the Starshatter Arsenal detachment, which adds 1 to Hit rolls against units near objectives and grants Assault to Vehicle and Mounted ranged weapons. The core engine is flooding every objective with threats simultaneously — Arks advance and fire without penalty, Wraiths and Ophydians teleport into scoring positions, while Flayed Ones disrupt backfield holds. Chrono-impedance Fields on the Silent King further taxes opponent action economy, rewarding lists that lean on elite melee to clear Necron objective campers. Where it struggles is against high-volume mortal wound output and durable screening armies that deny its infiltrators from reaching objectives before the Arks can punish defenders.
530: Built around Allarus Custodians, Vertus Praetors, Shield-Captains in both Allarus armour and on Dawneagle jetbikes, Witchseekers, Blade Champions, Custodian Guard, and Custodian Wardens, this Lions Of The Emperor list enforces a strict spacing discipline — every non-Vehicle unit that fights or shoots alone gains +1 to hit and +1 to wound, rewarding deliberate isolation over massed formations. The win condition is controlled aggression: spread units across the board to simultaneously trigger that lone-wolf bonus, contest objectives with durable golden bodies, and delete priority targets through layered combat and shooting pressure. It punishes low-model-count elite armies hardest, because those lists struggle to contest every isolated Custodian simultaneously while absorbing lethal, buffed output from multiple angles. Dense screening armies and anything generating overlapping auras can drag units into proximity of each other, shutting off the detachment bonus and blunting the list's entire damage engine.
525: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, Ravenwing Command Squads, Outriders, and Black Knights, with Sammael, Lion El'Jonson, and Azrael providing command weight — all operating under Company of Hunters and the Darkflight Pursuit enhancement, which gives RAVENWING FLY units Ignores Cover on all ranged attacks. The engine is relentless mobile fire: Company of Hunters lets every unit shoot after falling back and lets MOUNTED units shoot after advancing, meaning the fleet never sits still — it advances onto objectives, dumps anti-armour and anti-infantry fire with Ignores Cover, then falls back out of combat without losing its shooting. This punishes gunlines and entrenched infantry hard, stripping cover saves while outpacing slower armies that rely on static defensive positioning. It cracks open against fast melee threats that can tag multiple speeders simultaneously, since the high unit count of fragile FLY platforms means a coordinated charge wave can bottleneck the fall-back-and-shoot engine before it generates enough output to stabilise.
529: Built around Grey Hunters, Blood Claws, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Scouts, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Logan Grimnar, Ragnar Blackmane, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, and Wolf Priests, this is a mass-infantry, mid-board brawler running Saga of the Beastslayer to grant Lethal Hits against Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles across the entire army the moment it contacts the enemy. The plan is to flood the midfield with cheap bodies doing actions while Grey Hunters — exempt from shooting restrictions during actions via Veterans of the Fang — maintain fire pressure, and the Headtakers and Terminators punch through elite targets with Lethal Hits fueling reliable damage without needing high AP. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that struggle to clear volume, where Lethal Hits on Monsters and Vehicles turns even mid-tier weapons into efficient anti-tank overload. Dense screens, strong objective-holding infantry blobs, and fast counter-charge units crack this list open by neutralising the action engine and bogging the brawlers before they can consolidate midfield control.
521: Built around Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams, Ghostkeels, Riptides, Broadsides, and Commander Shadowsun operating under Advanced Acquisition Cadre and Kauyon, this list leans on hidden shooting — Stealth Battlesuits and Pathfinder Teams fire without breaking concealment — then transitions into a Kauyon-fueled late-game firepower spike from rounds three through five, where everything gains Sustained Hits 1 and Guided units ignore modifiers when targeting Spotted enemies. The win condition is attrition: screen with Piranhas and Vespid Stingwings to deny forward pressure, accumulate mid-game objective presence, and then overwhelm with amplified shooting once Kauyon activates. It punishes slow, durable armour-heavy lists by combining mobile anti-armour tools with the late-round damage multiplier to crack tough targets that other armies would stall against. Lists that alpha-strike the screening layer early or flood the midboard before Kauyon comes online deny it the time it needs to snowball.
441: Built around Librarians (both on foot and in Terminator armour), Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, Sternguard Veterans, and screening infantry in Scouts and Intercessors, this is a psychic-amplified elite infantry list running the Librarius Conclave alongside the Unforgiven Task Force. The engine is the Conclave's round-by-round Discipline selection — cycling Divination for reroll stacking on Sternguard or Companions, Biomancy for repositioning, and Pyromancy for board control — while the Unforgiven Task Force keeps Battle-shocked units holding objectives at OC 1 and pumps a key unit's OC each Command phase. It punishes gunline-heavy armies by layering rerolls onto already-efficient elite shooting and melee, making damage output remarkably consistent against static or low-mobility opponents. However, the list's reliance on multiple expensive characters and small elite units leaves it vulnerable to alpha-strike pressure that bypasses screening infantry and removes the Psykers before the Discipline engine can fire.
550: Built around multiple Lords of Change, Kairos Fateweaver, Be'lakor, and fast-moving Screamers and Flamers, this is an elite, highly mobile Tzeentch-heavy daemon force running Lords Of The Warp with Scintillating Legion as its secondary detachment. The Flux token engine from Scintillating Legion fuels re-rolls on key Hit, Wound, and Damage rolls for Tzeentch units, letting Lords of Change and Flamers punch dramatically above their raw stats while Screamers and Flamers sweep across the board to burn out light infantry and secure mid-table objectives. It punishes armies built around fragile elite infantry and static backfield gunlines, as the combination of mobile anti-armour, layered lethal output, and re-roll consistency overwhelms lists that cannot project board-wide threat. Durability-focused armies that can weather the initial offensive surge and answer multiple Lords of Change simultaneously will grind it down, since the list has limited bodies to absorb attrition once its key threats are neutralised.
551: Built around Skarbrand, multiple Rendmasters on Blood Throne, Bloodcrushers, Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, and a supporting screen of Nurglings and Plaguebearers, this is a Blood Legion list that weaponises reactive surge movement — each time an enemy unit ends a move within 8" of a Khorne Daemon, one of those units surges D6" forward, threatening to cascade charge opportunities across the whole front. The win condition is layered lethality through overwhelming melee volume: Bloodletters and Flesh Hounds flood mid-table objectives while Skarbrand and Bloodthirsters serve as catastrophic kill-pieces that reward the opponent for retreating and punish them for staying. It brutally punishes horde and medium-armour lists that cannot disengage cleanly, since every fall-back creates a new surge trigger and fresh charge eligibility. Elite, low-model armies with strong shooting that can kite or alpha-strike the Khorne centrepiece before it closes distance can break the engine before it fires.
459: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ variants (Battle Tank and Exterminator), Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks, and Tech-Priest Enginseers, this is a mechanised armoured column running the Designation Force detachment, where Scout Sentinels and Infantry Smoke units plant Signal Flares to paint targets for the rest of the fleet. The win condition is layered designation fire: Sentinels sprint forward to mark high-value threats, then the massed Squadron guns delete them from the gunline, with Hellhounds covering flanks and burning out infantry screens that would otherwise block line of sight. This build punishes armour-heavy and elite lists brutally — stacking Squadron volume fire against expensive targets it has already designated strips even durable vehicles efficiently. It cracks open against fast aggressive armies that can swamp the Sentinels before flares land, collapsing the designation chain and leaving the static gunline shooting blind into a melee it cannot escape.
465: Built around Daemonettes, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors, Tormentors, and Rhinos, this list runs the Carnival of Excess detachment to keep Emperor's Children and Legions of Excess units within 6" of each other, generating the Empowered state and its Sustained Hits across virtually every combat unit on the board. The game plan is to flood the midtable with an Empowered horde — Rhino-delivered Infractors and Tormentors pushing objectives while Defilers provide mobile anti-armour punch and Lords Exultant (frequently carrying Possessed Blade and Warp Walker) amplify the kill chain. It punishes infantry-heavy and mid-density lists badly, because Sustained Hits stacks into overwhelming volume of attacks that clears screens and grinds brawlers simultaneously. Spread-out elite armies that deny the 6" Empowered bubble — or gunlines that delete key pieces before the Rhinos arrive — break the synergy and leave the individual units underperforming.
546: Built around the Void Dragon, the Nightbringer, and Immortals backed by Flayed Ones, this list fields multiple C'tan Shards as its primary offensive engine under the Hand of the Dynasty detachment, which grants Immortals and Warriors Assault on their ranged weapons — letting those units advance and still shoot while remaining eligible to perform actions. The win condition is sustained mid-field pressure: C'tan Shards threaten durable melee targets while Assault-equipped Immortals push up aggressively, scoring secondaries without sacrificing firepower. It punishes slower, low-mobility armies that can't contest the middle of the board, as the list's combination of hard-to-shift Shards and action-completing infantry creates an almost unanswerable objective presence. However, high-volume, high-AP shooting that focuses the Shards individually can dismantle the damage engine, and lists with fast enough threat projection to bubble-wrap objectives early leave the Immortal core without room to work.
544: Built around multiple Skorpekh Lord-led Skorpekh Destroyer units, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Nekrosor Ammentar, Illuminor Szeras, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers under Lokhust Lords, the Silent King, and Ophydian Destroyers, this Awakened Dynasty list weaponizes the detachment's +1 to Hit across nearly every combat and shooting unit on the table. The win condition is layered threat saturation — Ophydians and Skorpekhs hunt infantry midboard while Lokhust Heavy Destroyers and the Void Dragon crack vehicles, with Enaegic Dermal Bond keeping lead characters alive long enough to cycle damage into scoring turns. It punishes lists with spread-out, mid-toughness targets that can't absorb simultaneous melee and heavy anti-armour pressure from multiple angles. Concentrated alpha-strike armies or elite high-damage output can strip the attached characters before the hit-bonus engine fires, unraveling the whole threat package.
526: Built around Lokhust Destroyers, Nekrosor Ammentar, Ophydian Destroyers, Lokhust Lords, the C'tan Shard of the Void Dragon, Lychguard, and the Overlord with Translocation Shroud, this is a multi-vector Necron murder machine that floods the board with fast, durable threat vectors across multiple phases. The plan is to overwhelm opponents by projecting lethal ranged pressure through Lokhust Destroyers and the Void Dragon while Ophydian Destroyers threaten sudden melee eruptions from unexpected angles, forcing opponents to defend multiple kill zones simultaneously rather than concentrating resources. Its high mobility toolkit punishes slower, static gunlines that can't reposition quickly enough to address threats from all directions at once. It cracks open against tight alpha-strike armies and anything capable of stripping the Lokhust Destroyers before they activate, since losing that ranged backbone early collapses the layered threat structure the entire plan depends on.
556: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, massed Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, Squighog Boyz, and a murderer's row of beastboss characters — all swinging under War Horde's blanket Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon — this is a wall of green bodies hitting like a freight train. The plan is to flood the midboard with chaff Gretchin screens and Trukk-delivered infantry, then crash character-buffed melee units into anything that contests objectives, generating obscene hit volume through Sustained Hits 1 to grind opponents off the table. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't absorb the sheer number of attacks coming from multiple threat vectors simultaneously, especially when Painboys keep key units fighting. Armies with strong shooting and board control at range can thin the horde before it arrives, and anything that pops Trukks in transit leaves expensive units exposed in the open.
558: Built around Wazdakka Gutsmek, massed Warbikers, Deffkoptas, Deffkilla Wartrikes, and Trukks backed by Gretchin screens, this is a wall of fast Ork metal that either runs Kult Of Speed — letting Speed Freeks shoot and charge after Advancing or Falling Back — or More Dakka! to give Infantry Assault on all ranged attacks. The win condition is flooding the mid-table on turn one, pinning opponents onto their objectives with vehicle bodies while Warbikers and Deffkoptas grind for kill secondaries and primary hold. It punishes static gun-line armies that lack the volume of anti-vehicle fire to stop multiple fast threats converging simultaneously from different angles. It cracks when faced with high-density anti-armour that can strip bikes in bunches before the brawl is established, leaving Gretchin as the only surviving objective holders.
533: Built around multiple Commanders in Coldstar Battlesuits, Crisis Sunforge and Starscythe Battlesuits, The Twin Lance, Commander Farsight, Stealth Battlesuits, Pathfinder Teams with Darkstrider, Broadsides, and Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits running Experimental Prototype Cadre plus Kauyon — every Battlesuit Character's guns reach 6" further, and from round three onward the whole force gains Sustained Hits 1 plus the ability to ignore modifiers when Guided units target Spotted enemies. It punishes durable, low-model-count elite armies that want to trade units slowly, because the Sustained Hits surge turns already efficient anti-armour firepower into an overload their saves cannot absorb. Armies that alpha strike before round three or flood the board with cheap screens crack it open, denying the Kauyon payoff window and blocking Pathfinder spot-chains before they mature.
561: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour buffing Scarab Occult Terminators and Rubric Marines, supported by waves of Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, and foot Sorcerers, this is a mass-infantry phalanx running the Rubricae Phalanx detachment. The plan is to flood mid-table with durable, AP-resistant bodies — Rubricae shrugging off all Damage 1 hits on an improved armour save — while Fatecaster Greatbows and Sekhetar Robots sustain skimmer fire to grind down opponents and hold objectives through attrition. It punishes lists that rely on high-volume low-damage shooting, since those attacks bounce off the detachment's core saving-throw buff and the sheer body count simply absorbs pressure. It cracks when faced with high-Damage, low-volume anti-tank firepower that bypasses the Damage 1 immunity entirely and removes expensive Terminator bricks in few hits.
560: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened, Sekhetar Robots buffed by Sorcerers (including Terminators), Scarab Occult Terminators, Rubric Marines, Daemon Princes, and Magnus the Red, this list runs the Hexwarp Thrallband detachment to project a Flow of Magic across No Man's Land whenever it controls half the midfield objectives, unlocking army-wide Psychic synergies — and pairs it with Sekhetar Cohort to grant Robots Psychic attacks and WS buffs from nearby Psykers. The win condition is layered, simultaneous pressure: Robots and Terminators brawl for midfield markers to trigger and sustain Flow of Magic while Enlightened and gunline elements delete screens, forcing opponents into no-win trades. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously against this volume of Psychic-tagged melee and ranged threat across every zone. It cracks open against fast alpha-strike lists that can collapse midfield control early and sever Flow of Magic before the kill engine comes online.
571: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, multiple Skorpius Disintegrators, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Onager Dunecrawlers, backed by dense screens of Skitarii Rangers and Servitor Batteclades under Lords Of The Forge — giving Tech-Priests a 4+ Invulnerable Save, Feel No Pain 5+, and the Baffling Data Screed ability to force enemy Vehicles to degrade mid-game. Armies that can reliably reach and tie up the firebase in melee — especially fast assault threats that can bypass or chew through the Ranger and Servitor screens — will crack the scoring engine before the gunline can delete them.
609: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, Blade Champion, Vertus Praetors, and a walker core of Telemon and Contemptor-Achillus Dreadnoughts supercharged by Might of the Moritoi's +2" Movement and +1 to advance and charge rolls, this list plays a highly mobile elite-infantry-and-walker hybrid under the Shield Host ka'tah framework. The plan is to push walkers and elite infantry into multiple threat corridors simultaneously, using superior melee reach to punish any opponent who cannot screen every angle, converting Blade Champion and dreadnought charges into devastating kill-chain sequences. The weakness is raw model count — concentrated shooting or alpha-strike lists can remove key walkers before their buffed movement pays off, and the build struggles to recover lost pieces efficiently.
584: Built around Krieg Combat Engineers, Tempestus Scions with Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Gaunt's Ghosts, Scout Sentinels, Krieg Heavy Weapons Squads, Cadian Recon Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, and Taurox transports, this is a mass-infantry gunline running the Designation Force detachment, with just over half of lists adding Siege Regiment's Creeping Barrage to punish distant enemy units with Shaken. The win condition is layering Signal Flares from Scout Sentinels and Sentinels onto priority targets, saturating them with coordinated small-arms and heavy weapons fire while a horde of cheap bodies contests objectives across the board. It punishes infantry-heavy lists through sheer volume of fire and attrition, denying movement with Creeping Barrage while Scions and Engineers apply focused pressure. It struggles against elite low-model-count armies that can methodically delete its key pieces before the numbers game overwhelms them.
610: Built around Custodian Guard, Custodian Wardens, Allarus Custodians, and Blade Champions as the armoured core, supported by Witchseekers and Prosecutors as the Anathema Psykana contingent, this Talons of the Emperor force blends elite melee infantry with a layered aura network — Null Aegis granting Feel No Pain 5+ against psychic attacks and mortal wounds to nearby Custodes, while Deadly Unity flows the other direction. The plan is to push durable, high-damage units into mid-board objectives while the mixed Custodes-Sisterhood bubble keeps both halves of the army mutually reinforced, grinding out primary points through sheer resilience. The crack is volume of conventional AP-2 or better shooting — the aura network requires tight clustering that well-placed blast weapons or high-volume anti-infantry fire can exploit brutally.
542: Built around Noise Marines, Chaos Bikers, Rhinos ferrying Chosen and Legionaries, Cultist Mobs for board coverage, Defilers, and Huron Blackheart with the Red Corsairs Raiders and Masters of the Maelstrom rounding out the core, this is a Renegade Raiders gunline-brawler hybrid that floods the mid-table. It punishes static gunlines and lightly screened armour-heavy lists, where mobile shooting with improved AP overwhelms anything relying on 3+ or 2+ saves to survive at range. It cracks open against elite melee armies with reliable alpha-strike reach — losing Rhinos or Bikers early collapses the mid-board presence before the AP bonus can do its work.
471: Built around War Dog Karnivores, Knight Despoilers, and Nurglings screens, Infernal Lance is a mobile heavy-armour blender that uses the Malefic Surge mechanic to Empower its Knights each Command phase — accepting the risk of mortal wounds for a significant offensive payoff. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot absorb the sheer volume of high-quality attacks across multiple giant threats simultaneously. Its weakness is attrition against armies that can strip its screening layer early and then kite or tarpit the Knights before they Surge, cracking open the list before its damage engine fires.
595: Built around Indomitor Kill Teams, Deathwatch Veterans, Terminator squads, and a Captain in Gravis Armour led by the Watch Master, this is a mixed-infantry gunline that leans hard into wound-normalization through the Black Spear Task Force's majority-Toughness rule, making its heterogeneous Kill Teams deliberately harder to efficiently wound. The plan is to saturate mid-table with durable, multi-profile units that grind scoring opportunities while the Watch Master and Tome of Ectoclades buff output against priority targets. It punishes heavy gunlines and massed hordes by presenting awkward wound thresholds across multiple units simultaneously, forcing opponents into inefficient target selection. It cracks open against fast aggressive pressure and alpha-strike builds that can isolate and delete individual squads before the layered durability can pay off.
575: Built around Hellions, Wyches, Reavers, Incubi, Mandrakes, and a dense fleet of Venoms and Raiders carrying Kabalite Warriors and Scourges, this list is a mass Wych Cult swarm running Exhibition Of Slaughter to give every melee unit Lethal Hits against non-Monster, non-Vehicle targets, layered with Skysplinter Assault so anything that disembarks gains Lance in melee and Ignores Cover on ranged weapons. The plan is to flood every quarter of the board with cheap bodies while Lelith Hesperax, Drazhar, and Succubi punch devastating kill-holes through infantry, generating pressure across all three lanes simultaneously rather than committing to a single threat vector. It punishes mid-tier infantry armies brutally — the combination of Lethal Hits into Lance on disembarking units shreds through anything that isn't armored, and sheer model volume makes tabling the screen nearly impossible. However, it struggles against heavy Vehicle and Monster spam, where the Lethal Hits exemption bites hard and Scourges alone cannot reliably carry the anti-armor workload.
541: Built around Warp Talons, Raptors, a jump-pack Chaos Lord, Cultist Mobs, and Defilers, this is an aggressive airborne pressure list that floods the midboard and flanks with flying infantry while Defilers provide heavy fire support from range. The win condition is attrition through momentum — the jump pack core strips units below half-strength or battle-shocks them, then layers on conditional hit re-rolls and hit penalties to punish weakened enemy units in subsequent combats and shooting. It punishes slow gunlines and horde armies hard, using its mass of mobile bodies to contest multiple objectives simultaneously while the Defilers threaten armour at range. However, it struggles against elite armies that resist being whittled down and against lists that can surgically delete the flying infantry before those conditional bonuses ever trigger.
588: Built around Flawless Blades, Infractors, Lord Exultants, Tormentors, Lucius the Eternal, Defilers, and winged Daemon Princes, this is a Peerless Bladesmen charge-engine that weaponizes the post-charge Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1 trigger to amplify close-combat output across the entire army. The plan is to deliver multiple units into combat simultaneously — Rhinos and on-foot screens pushing Flawless Blades into range while Defilers and Daemon Princes create secondary threat vectors — then use Spectacle of Slaughter's Fights First on Flawless Blades to punish any counter-charge. It punishes elite melee armies that rely on weathering the charge, since Fights First strips the initiative advantage and Lethal Hits makes even moderate attack volumes lethal against high-save targets. Gunlines and screens that prevent the charge entirely — or fast anti-tank that kills Defilers and Daemon Princes before engagement — deflate the engine before it fires.
592: Built around Purifier Squads, Castellan Crowe, Grand Master Nemesis Dreadknights, Strike Squads, and Interceptors, this is a mobile infantry-heavy force that expands its Hallowed Ground across the table by pushing Purifiers into No Man's Land and contesting objectives. 591: Built around Paladin Squads, Strike Squads, Brotherhood Terminator Squads, a Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight, Interceptor Squads, and Brotherhood Chaplains, this is a mobile psychic melee army running the Argent Assault detachment, with Banishers available as a secondary detachment in most lists. It cracks open against swarm armies and elite infantry that can flood the defensive line with bodies, denying foundation control through sheer volume and exploiting the list's limited ability to clear cheap screening units efficiently.
580: Built around Doomsday Arks, Flayed Ones, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers, and the C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer, this list plants heavy artillery in a protected backfield castle while mobile threats roam forward to threaten objectives and key targets. Flayed Ones provide aggressive board pressure and objective harassment, forcing opponents to either overcommit to chasing them or cede ground to the castle. The build punishes slow, durable armies that want to grind forward into ranged fire, but aggressive alpha-strike lists that close distance quickly can outpace the damage output and crack the firebase before the heavy guns can answer.
604: Built around Ghazghkull Thraka, multiple Warbosses, Boyz, Nobz, Stormboyz, and Breaka Boyz hauled forward in Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a War Horde list that puts Sustained Hits 1 on every Ork melee weapon in the army. 601: Built around massed Boyz squads, multiple Warbosses, Ghazghkull Thraka, Painboys keeping bodies alive, and Big Mek Dakkarigs and Wazdakka Gutsmek rounding out the command structure, this is a War Horde list that blankets the table with green bodies and charges everything into melee, where every Ork model's weapons gain Sustained Hits 1. 605: Built around Meganobz, Warboss and Warboss in Mega Armour, Ghazghkull Thraka, Nobz, and Boyz packed into Trukks and Battlewagons, this is a freight-train melee army that floods the mid-table with armoured fists. It punishes static or slow-moving lists that can't prevent contact, as overlapping transport mobility and sheer model volume make screening a nightmare. It cracks apart against armies that can strip transports at range before the Waaagh! lands, stranding elite infantry in the open and removing the delivery mechanism entirely.
602: Built around Gretchin screens, Boyz hordes, Flash Gitz, Lootas, Tankbustas, and Ghazghkull Thraka with Wazdakka Gutsmek leading a Trukk-mounted delivery package, this is a Freebooter Krew list that floods the mid-table with bodies while layering Sustained Hits 1 onto every shot across Infantry, Mounted, and Walker units, amplified further by More Dakka giving all Infantry ranged attacks Assault. It punishes static gunlines and light-vehicle spam by drowning them in volume fire that scales lethally once Waaagh! is live, with Painboys keeping key blobs functional through the counter-punch. Anything that can neutralise Ghazghkull early or deny mid-board presence through elite melee threats collapses the scoring engine before Waaagh! comes online.
598: Built around Trygons, Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, Von Ryan's Leapers, Lictors, and Neurolictors flooding the board from every angle, supported by Biovores, Zoanthropes, and a Neurotyrant synapse web, with the Swarmlord and The Red Terror providing elite punch — this is a Subterranean Assault list that weaponises the Burrower keyword to deliver multiple subsurface threats simultaneously, with Trygons frequently upgraded to Characters via the detachment rule and equipped with Trygon Prime or Tremor Senses enhancements. The win condition is coordinated disruption: infiltrators and deep strikers deny enemy positioning while Ravener packets brawl through the midtable and Biovores chip screening units, creating scoring lanes rather than simply contesting them. It punishes slow, high-value armies that struggle against multi-vector pressure, trading unfavourably against elite gunlines when they are force-multiplied across too many threat vectors to cover simultaneously. Armies with strong alpha-strike potential or tight deep-strike denial can collapse the plan before the subsurface wave lands, and the swarm's relatively fragile individual units crack apart against high-volume, low-AP shooting that bypasses the coordination the Neurotyrant provides.
607: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines in Chaos Rhinos, Tzaangors, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, Mutalith Vortex Beasts, and a supporting cast of Sorcerers, Infernal Masters, and Exalted Sorcerers, this is the Grand Coven detachment's layered psychic shooting engine at full expression. Hyper-elite or alpha-strike lists that can remove Magnus early and collapse the threat pyramid before the Grand Coven rotation delivers value crack this army open.
485: Built around Norn Emissaries, Norn Assimilators, Maleceptors, Tyrannofexes, Exocrines, Biovores, and the Swarmlord, this is a wall of Tyranid Monsters operating under Crusher Stampede — healthy units hold objectives at boosted OC while damaged ones hit and wound more reliably, creating a perverse incentive where attrition actually sharpens the claws. It punishes slow, low-mobility elite lists that can't contest multiple large-footprint monsters simultaneously, especially those lacking the anti-tank volume to drop several T10+ targets in a single round. Armies that can alpha-strike two or three key pieces turn one, or that flood cheap bodies to contest objectives and neutralize the OC advantage, expose how commit-heavy and low-model-count this roster truly is.
565: Built around Jakhals screening for Defilers, Forgefiends, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Exalted Eightbound under the Brazen Engines detachment, this is a mobile daemon-vehicle brawler that floods the table with layered threats at every point cost. The win condition is anti-armour overload — Defilers and Forgefiends crack hard targets from range and up close while the Eightbound and Slaughterbound surge into melee, with the Daemon Prince of Khorne directing the kill chain and Terror of Khorne forcing battle-shock rolls on anything they engage. It punishes armies that rely on a small number of elite or armoured units, stacking mobile anti-armour vectors that can't all be answered simultaneously. Armies with high volume, cheap screening, or strong shooting that can strip the Eightbound brick before it connects will crack this list open before the melee engine ever gets rolling.
719: Built around Repentia Squads, Arco-Flagellants, Celestian Sacresants, Hospitallers, Paragon Warsuits, Ministorum Priests, Battle Sisters in Rhinos, Palatine, Intranzia Fraye, Morvenn Vahl, and the Triumph of Saint Katherine, all running under the Penitent Host detachment with Sacred Champions alongside it, this is a mass melee horde that cycles Vows of Atonement each round to turbocharge whichever wave is hitting that turn. It punishes infantry-dense and medium-armour lists that can't absorb repeated high-volume close-combat waves before the Hospitallers patch the horde back together. Armies with long-range high-AP shooting or screens deep enough to deny charge lanes can bleed it out before the Vows start stacking meaningful advantages.
710: Built around witchseekers, Caladius grav-tanks, and a deep bench of Contemptor-Achillus, Telemon, Contemptor-Galatus, and Venerable Contemptor dreadnoughts running Silent Hunters with Solar Spearhead as a secondary detachment, this list floods the board with elite walkers backed by Anathema Psykana infantry. It punishes army designs built around elite elite infantry or mid-table objective holders, where the sheer volume of heavy dreadnought attacks combined with mobile tank presence overloads threat saturation. The weakness is concentrated high-AP shooting or anti-armour overload that can strip dreadnoughts below Starting Strength early, degrading the Solar Spearhead OC bonus before it can lock down primaries.
717: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Celestian Sacresants, and a deep bench of infantry packed into Immolators and Castigators, this is a mobile firebase that deliberately bleeds to get stronger — the Hallowed Martyrs detachment grants +1 to Hit when a unit is below Starting Strength, and adds +1 to Wound once it drops Below Half-strength, turning attrition into offensive output. The win condition is controlled sacrifice: screen with expendable units, absorb return fire, then unleash boosted volleys and melee charges from depleted-but-supercharged units while Celestian Insidiants and Arco-flagellants contest and threaten mid-board objectives. It punishes aggressive armies that feed it casualties early, as enemy alpha strikes and trade-focused lists inadvertently trigger the damage buffs at the worst possible moment. Armies that can efficiently delete full squads rather than chip them — preventing the detachment bonus from ever activating — or that out-range the Immolator skimmer screen entirely, expose how fragile this build is before the feedback loop kicks in.
662: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Hellhounds, Scout Sentinels, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this is a deep-strike gunline that weaponises the Bridgehead Strike detachment's rule granting +1 to hit rolls for units that arrive and immediately shoot. The win condition is dropping Scions and Command Squads into optimal angles each turn, stacking hit bonuses to delete priority targets while Engineers, Sentinels, and Hellhounds flood midboard objectives with bodies and flame. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot screen against repeated deep-strike waves landing with near-guaranteed hit rolls. Against fast aggressive armies that can pressure its static gunline elements and deny safe landing zones, the repeated repositioning becomes inefficient and the relatively fragile infantry bleeds points quickly.
693: Built around massed Crusader Squads surging behind Crusade Ancients, Bladeguard Veterans screened by Bladeguard Ancients, Intercessors, Scouts, and Grimaldus in the Vindication Task Force, this is a grinding infantry-horde army that floods objectives with bodies while layering Ancient-based durability across the whole force. The win condition is attrition and board control — Ancient units sitting on objectives become frustratingly hard to shift through the wound-roll penalty against higher-Strength attacks, while Crusader Squads use surge moves to rapidly reinforce contested markers. It punishes mid-range shooting lists that rely on high-Strength volume fire, since those are precisely the attacks the Ancient bubble-wrap neutered. It cracks against either elite melee that can bypass the wound modifier entirely with matched Toughness, or precision alpha strikes that can isolate and delete Ancients before the defensive layer is established.
645: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Jump Pack Captains, Scout Squads, and Intercessor Squads, this is a mobile, multi-threat Blood Angels force that floods the table with fast-moving elite infantry backed by durable objective holders. The win condition is layering aerial pressure from Sanguinary Guard onto midfield objectives while Scouts and Intercessors anchor scoring, forcing opponents to split resources between the threatening jump infantry and the entrenched ground game. It punishes slower, low-model-count armies that cannot contest multiple angles simultaneously, with the Guard's combination of mobility and melee output making it brutally efficient against elite infantry lists that lack volume screening. It cracks open when faced with heavy melee chaff or strong alpha-strike armies that can tag the Guard before they engage, stripping the offensive engine before it finds its charge.
667: Built around Bloodcrushers, Lords of Change, Screamers, and Be'lakor, this Cavalcade of Chaos list weaponizes the detachment's core rule — LEGIONES DAEMONICA MOUNTED units that fall back can still shoot and charge — to create a frictionless cavalry engine that never truly locks down. It punishes slower, low-mobility armies that cannot disengage from the fall-back-and-charge loop, turning every combat phase into a tax the opponent cannot escape. It cracks open when faced with high-volume, short-range shooting that can delete mounted units before they fall back, stripping the engine of the very pieces the whole interaction depends on.
666: Built around Beasts of Nurgle, Great Unclean Ones, Rotigus, and Plaguebearers, this list layers Nurgle's durability across multiple threat profiles — bloated monsters anchoring the midfield while infantry screens absorb pressure and bleed opponents dry. The win condition is attrition through lethal contact: Beasts of Nurgle crash into opposing units as mobile, self-regenerating brawlers while Great Unclean Ones and Rotigus grind through anything that survives, with the detachment's Deep Strike flexibility keeping opponents guessing on threat angles. It punishes elite low-model armies that cannot generate enough attacks to chew through stacked toughness and layered wound profiles before the scoring clock runs out. It cracks open against fast, high-volume damage that bypasses durability entirely — armies that can isolate and delete Beasts before they make contact leave the list's scoring engine offline.
668:

664: Built around Beasts of Nurgle, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, Plaguebearers, Nurglings, a Rendmaster on Blood Throne, a Great Unclean One, a Bloodthirster, and Be'lakor across the Cavalcade of Chaos detachment, this is a layered mixed-arms Daemon warband that blends Khorne cavalry with Nurgle attrition across every phase. 665: Built around Plaguebearers, Nurglings, and Beasts of Nurgle as a suffocating objective-holding mass, supported by Flesh Hounds as fast harassment screens, Be'lakor as an elite dark-magic disruptor, and a Bloodthirster as the primary kill piece. 653: Built around Venomcrawlers, Defilers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, Warpsmiths, Cultist Mobs, and Chaos Bikers, this is a daemon-engine swarm that floods the board with mid-weight armoured threats across primarily the Soulforged Warpack detachment, using Dark Pacts to spike Daemon Vehicles into +1 to wound and +2 Attacks simultaneously.
