The plan is to identify a priority threat early, stack Oath of Moment wound re-rolls onto it through Lysander's enhanced version, and bulldoze it off objectives while Terminator bricks hold ground and jump infantry contest flanks. It punishes armies that rely on a single powerful anchor — monsters, vehicles, elite infantry blocks — because concentrating the re-roll engine on one target makes that unit collapse disproportionately fast. It struggles against fast, spread-out armies that deny clean Oath of Moment focus and can kite the slow Terminator core, bleeding it for points across multiple objectives before it can consolidate.
528: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, and a Wolf Guard Battle Leader supported by massed Grey Hunters, this is a close-range brawling force running Saga Of The Great Wolf with Veterans Of The Fang in most lists. The engine is cycling Hunting Packs each Command phase to buff the whole force — re-rolls on Advances and Charges to close distance, then switching to other Packs to sustain the pressure — while Grey Hunters split into smaller five-man units to hold objectives and perform actions without sacrificing shooting. It punishes infantry-heavy midboard lists by drowning them in elite melee output and objective presence simultaneously, making it nearly impossible to trade efficiently. It cracks when facing high-volume anti-tank or alpha-strike armies that can kneecap the heavy hitters before the brawl begins.
614: Built around multiple Crisis suit variants — Starscythes, Sunforges, and Fireknives — stacked alongside Coldstar and Enforcer Commanders, Commander Farsight, and The Twin Lance, this is an all-battlesuit murder machine running Retaliation Cadre to squeeze bonus Strength and AP out of every short-range engagement. The win condition is simple and brutal: close to within 8–12" where the detachment ability kicks in, then unload overwhelming multi-role firepower to delete priority targets and bully mid-table objectives through raw combat presence. It punishes armour-heavy lists mercilessly, as the AP and Strength buffs at close range turn Crisis suits into anti-tank overload tools that most vehicles and monsters cannot absorb. The critical weakness is anything that can deny or punish the advance into close range — alpha-strike threats, deep strike denial, or fast melee armies that make short-range positioning catastrophically dangerous.
599: Built around Neurolictors, Lictors, Genestealers, Broodlords, Von Ryan's Leapers, Hyperadapted Raveners, and Raveners, this is a deep-strike-heavy assassination and midboard-brawl swarm running the Ambush Predators detachment, with most lists also adding Vanguard Onslaught to unlock Deathleaper as Warlord. The win condition is flooding the midboard with deep-striking threats simultaneously — Lictors and Neurolictors drop in with hit-roll rerolls against Characters to hunt down key pieces while Genestealers and Broodlords crash into whatever is left exposed, with Biovores providing backline chip pressure. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot screen every deep-strike vector, stranding opponent responses while multiple lethal units emerge from reserve in concert. It cracks open against dense screening forces or armies with strong overwatch and anti-deep-strike tools that can absorb the arrival wave and trade efficiently back into the light-wound profiles.
515: Built around Biovores, Tyrannofex, Exocrine, Genestealers, Broodlord, Hormagaunts, Maleceptor, Norn Emissary, Lictor, Neurotyrant, and Neurolictor, this is Invasion Fleet's sprawling combined-arms swarm — a mobile toolbox that brings shooting, melee, and synapse support in nearly every slot. The plan is to threaten multiple vectors simultaneously: Genestealers and Broodlord apply savage melee pressure while Tyrannofex and Exocrine grind down mid-range targets, with Lictors and Neurolictor enabling deep-strike and board control to dictate engagement on favourable terms. It punishes low-model-count armies that struggle to hold multiple objectives, overwhelming them with layered threats that can't all be screened out. It cracks under focused, efficient anti-elite shooting that strips the expensive melee packages before they close, leaving the gunline elements exposed on objectives without sufficient board presence to compensate.
612: Built around Slaughterbound, Eightbound, Exalted Eightbound, a Daemon Prince of Khorne, and Jakhals screening the advance, this is a wall of World Eaters Possessed infantry that uses Brazen Fury — surging up to D6" after taking casualties in the enemy Shooting phase — to punish any opponent who tries to shoot it off objectives before it reaches combat. The win condition is mid-table pressure: Jakhals hold ground and absorb punishment while the Possessed wave closes distance, with the Daemon Prince leveraging Vessels of Wrath to punch through armour with Cleave or improved AP on the turn it matters. It excels against armies that rely on volume shooting to stall melee threats, since every casualty in the Shooting phase accelerates the charge rather than preventing it. It cracks open against boards with reliable long-range high-damage output that can wipe full squads before Brazen Fury triggers, or against deep-strike denial lists that box it into its own deployment zone and starve it of the mid-table brawl it needs.
708: Built around Allarus Custodians, Caladius Grav-Tanks, Witchseekers, Custodian Guard, a Blade Champion, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this list splits between Tharanatoi Hammerblow's ingress-then-charge threat with Terminators and Solar Spearhead's vehicle OC-boosting presence. The plan is to layer threat vectors — tanks parking on objectives at elevated OC while Allarus and the Shield-Captain ingress to threaten charges — forcing opponents to answer multiple problems simultaneously. It punishes slow, durable armies that cannot redeploy quickly, as the combination of high-OC vehicles and hard-hitting Terminator drops overwhelms static defenders. It cracks open against aggressive early pressure and elite melee armies that can strip vehicles below Starting Strength before the OC and hit-roll benefits have done their work.
723: Built around Sydonian Dragoons with taser lances, Ironstrider Ballistarii, Sicarian Infiltrators, Skitarii Rangers, Skorpius Disintegrators, and Belisarius Cawl supported by Thulia Ghuld, this list blends a fast cavalry hammer with a patient ranged platform. The plan is to use Infiltrators and Rangers to hold and screen midfield objectives while Dragoons threaten decisive mid-table brawls and Ballistarii strip armour from range, generating board control that translates directly into primary points. It punishes slower, armor-heavy lists that cannot clear layered infantry screens before the Dragoons close and the Ballistarii cycle fire. However, high-volume shooting that can simultaneously delete the cavalry screen and pressure the gunline exposes how little redundancy sits between the Dragoons dying early and the scoring engine stalling out.
492: Built around Allarus Custodians, Custodian Guard, Blade Champion, Vertus Praetors, Custodian Wardens, Witchseekers, and a Shield-Captain in Allarus Terminator Armour, this list runs the Shield Host detachment — with Tharanatoi Hammerblow layered on top in three-quarters of lists to give Terminator units a charge re-roll after an ingress move — creating a mobile, multi-threat elite force with exceptional unit quality across every battlefield role. The win condition is flexible pressure: the Ka'tah system toggles between Critical Hit fishing on melee attacks and improved Armour Penetration, letting the list dial in the right kill profile each round while Vertus Praetors and Witchseekers contest objectives and Allarus Custodians drop in to punish exposed targets. It excels against lists that rely on medium-durability multi-wound infantry, where high-AP melee and layered lethality systematically delete key pieces before opponents can respond. Horde armies and shooting-dominant lists with long-range anti-tank can crack it open — screening neutralises the ingress threat and volume fire tests the relatively small model count.
439: Built around Skitarii Marshals, Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, Tech-Priest Manipuluses, and waves of Rangers, Hastarii Fusiliers, Vanguard, and Sicarian Infiltrators piling out of Skorpius Duneriders, this is a transport-delivered horde running primarily under Lords of the Forge, which layers 4+ invulnerable saves and Feel No Pain 5+ onto its Tech-Priests while Baffling Data Screed chips enemy vehicles from close range. The plan is to flood midboard objectives with cheap, layered bodies transported into position, grinding through attrition while Ironstrider Ballistarii and Servitor Battleclades add suppressive fire from behind the wave. It punishes lists that rely on low-volume, high-value shooting — spreading damage across a mass of cheap infantry and FNP-protected characters makes efficient killing extremely difficult. Blast weapons, mortal wound output, and anything that can strip transports before deployment punish it hard, collapsing the delivery mechanism and stranding infantry in the open.
741: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Kasrkin, Gaunt's Ghosts, Ursula Creed, Scout Sentinels, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, and Krieg Combat Engineers, this is a dense infantry gunline that deep strikes elite kill units while flooding the board with expendable bodies. The plan is to use Scions dropped via deep strike for mobile anti-armour and skimmer fire while the horde of Shock Troops, Kasrkin, and Engineers holds objectives and bricks midfield under Command Squad orders. It punishes armies that cannot clear bodies efficiently, trading cheap infantry for scoring turns while elite units pick apart key targets from unexpected angles. Concentrated high-damage shooting or strong melee that can crack through the screening infantry and suppress the Command Squad order chain before the Scions land will expose how fragile individual units are once isolated.
461: Built around wave after wave of Plaguebearers, Great Unclean Ones, Rotigus, Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Sloppity Bilepipers, Poxbringers, and Epidemius operating under Plague Legion, this is a suffocating attrition horde that drowns the midboard in diseased bodies. The engine is Shadow of Chaos — parking Nurgle units within 9" of everything forces mandatory Battle-shock tests every Command phase, degrading enemy unit efficiency while Warptide lets Battleline units advance-and-charge to flood objectives without sacrificing pressure. It punishes elite low-model-count armies brutally, as forced Battle-shock cascades strip Ld-dependent abilities while sheer wound volume overwhelms focused firepower. Armies with reliable Battle-shock immunity or high-mobility deep-strike threats can sidestep the Shadow bubble entirely and pick apart the flanks before the horde can smother them.
586: Built around waves of Daemonettes, Fiends, Beasts of Nurgle, Keepers of Secrets, the Contorted Epitome, the Tormentbringer, and the Masque of Slaanesh, this list weaponises both Legion Of Excess and Warptide to create a perpetual-motion assault engine: Daemonettes advance and still charge, Fell Back units re-engage the same turn, and nothing ever truly disengages. The win condition is layered combat pressure across every zone simultaneously — flooding objectives with expendable Daemonette screens while Fiends and Keepers hunt anything that contests, making it nearly impossible to hold a safe position anywhere on the board. It punishes slow, castle-style armies brutally, as the advance-and-charge loop denies breathing room and lets the list trade efficiently into anything that tries to sit on objectives. The weakness is volume of quality anti-infantry fire before the first charge lands — a list that can thin Daemonettes at range disrupts the screen math and leaves flanks exposed to counterplay.
747: Built around War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Brigands — six to eight fast, aggressive light Knights swarming the board with overlapping threat vectors. The plan is to pick apart opposing armies piece by piece using mobile anti-armour pressure across multiple activation windows, with Infernal Lance's Malefic Surge or Houndpack Lance's Sustained Hits 1 focus-fire funneling concentrated damage onto priority targets each turn. The sheer volume of durable, fast chassis punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot answer eight separate threat sources simultaneously, forcing unfavorable trades across the entire field. The build cracks under high-volume anti-tank lists that can efficiently strip individual War Dogs before they activate, since losing even two early collapses the activation economy the entire engine depends on.
750: Built around swarms of Cultist Mobs backed by a flexible menagerie of Chaos Knights, this list uses Iconoclast Fiefdom to splice up to 500 points of Damned CSM units — primarily those Cultist Mobs — into what is otherwise a Knight army. The Cultists flood objectives and absorb early damage while the Knights generate lethal anti-armour pressure from range and in melee, using the Lords of Dread sub-detachment (present in roughly six in ten lists) to pump Chaos Knight Character OC and free Claimed for the Dark Gods triggers. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that cannot contest multiple objectives simultaneously, as the Cultist screen forces opponents to commit to clearing chaff while Knights pick apart armour and heavy infantry. Horde armies that generate sufficient small-arms volume can strip the Cultist screen cheaply, exposing the Knights to being isolated and overwhelmed by anti-tank overload before the scoring engine can recover.
727: Built around Chaos Terminators, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, Cultist Mobs, and Defilers, the Cabal of Chaos is a Dark Pact-fuelled mid-table brawler that trades survivability for amplified psychic firepower and melee threat. The engine is the Cabal of Chaos detachment rule: Psyker units that make a Dark Pact gain +1 Strength on ranged attacks, and Daemon Princes that Dark Pact gain a melee bonus, so the list chains Pacts turn after turn to punch above its stats while Cultist screens protect the expensive core. About half of lists add Obliterators and around a third add Warpstrike Champions to redeploy Terminators and Mutilators off the board end-of-turn, threatening any flank. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that can't strip screens fast enough, but concentrated high-Strength shooting — the kind that triggers the Pact's self-damage risk repeatedly — and elite assault armies that can breach the screen and lock Psykers in combat before they fire can unravel the whole chain.
729: Built around Chaos Bikers, Cultist Mobs, Traitor Guardsmen, Defilers, and Chaos Rhinos operating under Pactbound Zealots, this list floods the board with cheap bodies while parking Daemon Engine firepower at range. The plan is to drown opponents in screening chaff — Cultists and Guardsmen holding flanks and objectives — while Defilers and Bikers threaten mobile anti-armour pressure and melee aggression backed by Lethal Hits on 5+ in combat. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear waves of expendable infantry before the Daemon Engines grind them down. However, it cracks under high-volume mortal wound output or strong anti-horde shooting that strips the chaff screens efficiently, leaving the heavier engines exposed and unsupported mid-table.
725: Built around Ravenwing Command Squads, Outrider Squads, Ravenwing Black Knights, Sammael, Land Speeder Vengeances, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Scout Squads operating under Company of Hunters, this is a hyper-mobile gunline that shoots after falling back and advances without losing firepower — every unit fires on every turn regardless of combat pressure. The win condition is relentless mid-table aggression: Ravenwing FLY units exploit Darkflight Pursuit's Ignores Cover to strip defended objectives clean while the Mounted keyword lets bikers advance-and-shoot into scoring positions, generating points through tempo and attrition rather than a single kill spike. It punishes castle-style gunlines and elite infantry lists that rely on staying stationary and holding cover, because neither defensive posture limits this army's damage output. It struggles against armies that can flood the mid-table with cheap bodies, denying the fast movers clean board presence and absorbing the anti-armour payload on chaff rather than key targets.
637: Built around a swarm of Land Speeder Vengeances, Land Speeders, and a Storm Speeder Thunderstrike — all supported by Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Scout Squads, and a Lieutenant with combi-weapon — this is a fast-moving, skimmer-heavy Dark Angels force with serious anti-armour punch. The plan is to use early board presence and mobile firepower to delete high-value targets while Scouts and Deathwing Knights contest objectives and generate OC where it matters. It punishes slow, armoured gunlines that can't respond to multi-angle skimmer threats, overloading anti-tank resources across a wide, mobile threat envelope. The weakness is staying power: without a defining detachment rule to lean on, it's fragile against fast aggressive armies that can crack the light-hulled speeders before they fire and deny the layered threat from ever materialising.
642: Built around Deathwing Knights (averaging two squads), Chaplain in Terminator Armour, Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Inner Circle Companions, and an Ancient in Terminator Armour, this is a terminator-heavy elite brawl list operating across either Wrath of the Rock or Interrogation Conclave detachments depending on the matchup. The win condition is getting durable, buffed terminator blobs into melee — Lion and the Chaplain chain-enabling Deathwing Knights and Inner Circle Companions to delete priority targets while Azrael keeps key units alive, converting raw durability into objective control through attrition. It punishes elite-model lists by making every Strength-over-Toughness wound roll harder through Wrath of the Rock's wound-roll subtraction, forcing anti-tank overload against models that simply don't fold. Horde armies and high-volume mid-strength shooting crack it open by flooding wound rolls too cheaply to be mitigated, overwhelming the elite model count with sheer output before the hammer units can engage.
726: Built around Azrael, Lion El'Jonson, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and a fast Ravenwing cavalry core of Sammael, Ravenwing Black Knights, Ravenwing Command Squad, and Outriders, this is a Wrath of the Rock list that blends elite terminator hammer-units with high-speed mounted pressure. The plan is to use the Ravenwing elements to contest and harass early while the Deathwing Knights and Companions crash into whatever the bikes have softened up, with Azrael and the Lion anchoring the midfield brawl and generating sustained combat threat. The -1 to Wound rolls against Strength-over-Toughness attacks makes the entire infantry and mounted core remarkably durable against the mid-strength weapons that typically shred marines, punishing opponents who lean on volume fire rather than dedicated high-damage tools. Lists that bring consistent high-Strength, low-volume anti-tank shooting can bypass that defensive modifier and pick apart the expensive elite units before the cavalry engine fully comes online.
636: Built around a swarm of Land Speeder Vengeances, standard Land Speeders, Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes, and Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes, all supercharged by multiple Librarians running the Librarius Conclave's round-by-round Psychic Discipline selection, with Inner Circle Companions, Scouts, Sternguard, and Azrael providing ground presence and screening. The engine is cycling Disciplines to match the phase — Divination's hit-and-wound re-rolls amplifying the speeder fleet's anti-armour output one turn, Biomancy pushing threat ranges the next — while the skimmer swarm maintains a mobile firebase that forces opponents to chase fast-moving targets across multiple vectors. This list punishes static gunlines and low-mobility forces that cannot reposition away from the constantly shifting optimal engagement range of the speeder fleet, and layered Apothecary support keeps key bodies on objectives longer than expected. Armies that can alpha-strike the fragile speeder chassis before Disciplines can be cycled, or that bring enough volume fire to strip multiple fast movers in a single shooting phase, expose how thin the survivability of the airborne core actually is.
629: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Lords of Contagion, Blightlord Terminators, Typhus, and Poxwalker screens, this is a slow-grinding Contagion-zone army that weaponizes the Death Lord's Chosen detachment's passive mortal wound engine — every Afflicted enemy unit rolls for D3 mortals each Command phase, steadily bleeding opponents across the game. The win condition is to push Lords of Contagion and Typhus deep into enemy lines, maximizing Contagion Range with Paragons of Putrescence's +3" buff to stack Afflicted triggers on as many units as possible while Deathshroud and Blightlords crush whatever survives. It punishes durable mid-tier infantry lists that expect to trade efficiently but instead hemorrhage mortal wounds while struggling to remove near-unkillable Terminator bodies. Fragile fast armies that stay outside Contagion range, or high-damage alpha strikers that can delete Lords before they spread Affliction, can gut the engine before it ever fires.
628: Built around Deathshroud Terminators, Poxwalkers, Lord of Contagion, Malignant Plaguecaster, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, Typhus, and Plague Marines operating under the Paragons of Putrescence detachment, which extends Death Guard Character Contagion Range by +3", this list drowns the mid-table in overlapping plague auras and durable bodies. The win condition is attrition through layered lethality — Contagion-boosted characters push debilitating auras across the board while Deathshroud and Blight-Haulers punish anything that tries to contest, generating points by holding mid while the opponent's units degrade faster than yours. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that can't efficiently clear tough multi-wound infantry and struggle to outpace the board-control established by massed Poxwalkers screening for lethal-aura characters. Horde armies with high activation counts or fast objective-runners that can stay outside Contagion range crack it open, as the entire engine depends on forcing enemies into the bubble rather than chasing them down.
701: Built around Deathwatch Veterans, Deathwatch Terminators, dual Librarians, and Intercessor squads, this is a mid-table shooting and brawling force that leans on Firestorm Assault Force in most lists to give its ranged weapons Assault and a Strength bump inside 12", turning aggressive repositioning into raw killing power. The plan is to push Terminators and Veterans forward behind Intercessor screens, close to within 12" to trigger that Strength bonus, and leverage Librarian psychic disciplines — Divination for re-rolls or Biomancy for movement — to crack priority targets and score through raw attrition. It punishes horde armies and gunlines hard, since the combination of high model-count screens, massed bolter volume, and close-range Strength bonuses overloads light-save and medium-save targets efficiently. It struggles against fast elite armies that can bypass the screen, isolate Terminators before they close, and avoid that 12" killzone entirely.
744: Built around Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, Maulerfiends, Defilers, Lords Exultant, Infractors in Rhinos, Tormentors, Noise Marines, and Flawless Blades, this Coterie of the Conceited list drives a wall of mobile threat into the mid-board every turn. The win condition is the Pact points engine: pledge an achievable kill count each round, cash it in consistently, and weaponize the accumulating Pact points to amplify the army's already punishing melee and anti-armour output. It punishes slower gunline and armour-heavy lists that cannot thin the wave of Maulerfiends and Princes before they hit combat, and the transported Infractors deny opponents clean objective holds. Lists that can alpha-strike the Princes and Maulerfiends off the board early disrupt the pledge math, leaving the slower infantry elements stranded without their kill-generating vanguard.
746: Built around Infractors (nearly three squads on average), Lords Exultant, Tormentors, Flawless Blades, Defilers, and Daemon Princes of Slaanesh with Wings, this is a high-volume melee army that uses Chaos Rhinos to deliver infantry into combat fast. The win condition is flooding mid-table with back-to-back melee threats — Infractors punch the line open, Defilers and Daemon Princes exploit the gaps, and Coterie of the Conceited rewards aggressive list-wide kill pledges with compounding Pact point generation. It punishes static gunlines and low-unit-count armies that cannot handle simultaneous pressure from multiple charging threat vectors across the board. It cracks open against elite screens and durable infantry blocks that survive the initial charge and deny the kill count needed to meet pledge thresholds, leaving the engine starved of Pact points and the army overextended.
743: Built around Flawless Blades, Noise Marines, Tormentors, Lord Kakophonists, and a winged Daemon Prince, this list runs the Spectacle of Slaughter detachment to give Flawless Blades Fights First, then ferries the bulk of its infantry forward in Chaos Rhinos to hit the midboard as a coordinated melee wave. The win condition is crashing charge-enabled units into contested objectives — Peerless Bladesmen rewards charging units with Lethal Hits or Sustained Hits 1, so the list scores by winning fights, holding ground, and denying the opponent's ability to trade efficiently. It punishes slower combat armies and horde infantry that can't survive Fights First pressure backed by high-volume melee output. It struggles against gunlines and alpha-strike lists that strip the Rhino transports before the charge lands, leaving the melee core exposed and reactive.
572: Built around Purestrain Genestealers, Aberrants, and their supporting cast of Abominants, Patriarch, and Biophagus, this is a mass-horde brawler running Biosanctic Broodsurge to stack extra Attacks onto charging claws and fists, while Xenocult Masses keeps Neophyte Hybrid screens healing back up inside terrain every Command phase. The win condition is a coordinated multi-wave assault — Genestealers and Aberrants hit in the same turn to overload opponent's fight-phase priority, with the charge bonus adding enough Attacks to erase elite units that expect to trade efficiently against single threats. It punishes lists with low model counts and fragile backlines by threatening every angle simultaneously, using Achilles Ridgerunners and Reductus Saboteurs to apply mobile anti-armour pressure while the melee tide advances. It struggles against armies that can reliably screen out charge lanes, deny terrain to the Neophyte bubble-wrap, or deliver enough high-volume shooting to strip squads below critical mass before the first wave lands.
754: Built around Grand Masters and Nemesis Dreadknights as the heavy-hitting centrepiece, supported by Strike Squads, Interceptors, Paladins, Brotherhood Terminators, and a Brotherhood Techmarine keeping the walkers operational, this list blends elite infantry depth with hard-to-shift walker muscle across a spread of detachments — Sanctic Spearhead's Advance-and-Assault movement and Hallowed Conclave's Fell Back-and-fire Terminators being the most common frames. The plan is to use Dreadknight mobility to threaten priority targets while infantry flood midboard objectives, with Interceptors surging after shooting to contest or screen, and Terminators punishing anyone who tries to disengage. It punishes slower, durable armies that rely on static fire lines, as the combination of advancing Dreadknights and repositioning infantry never gives those lists a clean target. Armies that can alpha-strike the Dreadknights off the table before Techmarine repairs trigger, or flood bodies to drown out the relatively low model count, will crack it open.
753: Built around Castellan Crowe, multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purifier Squads, Strike Squads, and Brotherhood Terminators, this Warpbane Task Force list uses Purifier positioning to physically extend Hallowed Ground across the midboard, layering objective control with a mobile elite infantry core. The win condition is map domination through Hallowed Ground saturation — Purifiers push into No Man's Land to unlock additional detachment benefits while Dreadknights provide fast-moving anti-armour punch and Crowe enables Purifier synergies. It punishes slow or static armies that cannot contest multiple midfield objectives simultaneously, as the combined threat range of Dreadknights and Terminators forces an opponent to defend everywhere at once. Highly mobile elite forces that can collapse individual Purifier squads — breaking Hallowed Ground coverage — and armies with sufficient long-range firepower to strip Dreadknights before they engage will crack this list open.
740:
Built around Deathwatch Kill Teams, Watch Masters, Imperial Navy Breachers, Subductor Squads, and a dense supporting cast of Inquisitors, Navigators, Rogue Trader Entourages, and Sisters of Battle embarked in Rhinos and Immolators, this is a massive transport-infantry swarm running Imperialis Fleet's command-phase targeting toggle to concentrate fire or lock down objectives on demand, with Veiled Blade doubling up Assassin special abilities for bonus pressure.

The plan is to flood the board with bodies across multiple transports, funnel the Eliminate At All Costs bonus into erasing priority threats while Subductor Squads and Breachers contest every corner, generating consistent primary through sheer volume.

It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot clear waves of cheap screening infantry fast enough to contest objectives.

Massed high-volume anti-infantry shooting and board-wide blasts crack it open, overwhelming the individual fragility of its many small units before the scoring engine gets rolling.
756: Built around multiple Grand Masters in Nemesis Dreadknights, Purgation Squads, Purifier Squads, and Castellan Crowe, this list runs either Fires of Purgation or Warpbane Task Force to layer psychic shooting pressure across the board. The plan is to pin enemy units with Righteous Persecution, forcing battle-shock rolls at -1, while Dreadknights threaten mobile anti-armour and Purifiers extend Hallowed Ground to contest mid-table objectives under favorable conditions. It punishes horde-heavy armies hardest, where massed psychic firepower and battle-shock cascades can strip bodies and deny actions simultaneously. It cracks open against elite low-model-count armies that shrug off battle-shock and can surgically remove Purgation Squads before the pinning engine comes online.
761: Built around Armiger Helverins, Armiger Warglaives, and a Knight Crusader, this list runs the Throne-Bonded Outriders detachment alongside Valourstrike Lance, turning every Advance move into a license to shoot — ranged weapons gain [ASSAULT] when the army moves, while Bondsman abilities layer [IGNORES COVER] onto Armiger shooting for a relentless, mobile fire platform. The win condition is anti-armour attrition at range: Helverins strip vehicles and monsters from distance with cover-ignoring autocannon volleys while Warglaives threaten anything that survives by closing aggressively, scoring through presence and denial rather than static holding. This punishes gunline and fortified armies hardest, since [IGNORES COVER] and [ASSAULT] together strip the defensive value of terrain that slower lists depend on. It cracks against elite melee threats and alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete individual Armigers before Bondsman synergies come online, as losing a key Armiger unit collapses the board presence the scoring engine relies on.
522: Built around four squads of Cthonian Beserks deep striking into close combat, supported by Berehk Stornbröw, Einhyr Hearthguard, Ûthar the Destined, Hernkyn Pioneers, Hernkyn Yaegirs, Hekaton Land Fortresses, and the Kapricus Carrier ferrying infantry forward, this is a Dêlve Assault Shift list that floods midfield with bodies and threatens lethal drop-charges from any angle. The win condition is overwhelming close-range pressure — Beserks materialize into your opponent's scoring units while Hearthguard and Fortresses lock down the midboard, forcing reactive play and stripping primary hold. It punishes slow, static gunlines that can't thin the screen fast enough before the deep strike lands, compounding the problem with sheer horde volume that outlasts most removal budgets. It cracks open against mobile armies with strong pre-game denial or fast chaff that bubble-wraps key units, strangling the Beserk drop and leaving the midfield brawl without its signature shock punch.
579: Built around Doomsday Arks, Canoptek Wraiths, Skorpekh Lords and Destroyers, Ophydian Destroyers, Flayed Ones, Hexmark Destroyers, Imotekh, Canoptek Reanimators, and Technomancers operating under Awakened Dynasty's +1 to Hit for CHARACTER-led units, this is a highly mobile toolbox army that floods the board with fast, resilient threats across every phase. The win condition is multi-vector pressure — Wraiths and Ophydians contest midfield while Destroyers hunt priority targets with character-boosted accuracy, Doomsday Arks crack armour at range, and Flayed Ones punish overextension. It excels against slower, static armies that struggle to handle simultaneous threats arriving from multiple angles before they can be prioritised and eliminated. However, high-volume mortal wound output or elite melee that bypasses reanimation can dismantle the layered durability, and a true alpha strike that removes the CHARACTER leaders collapses the hit-bonus engine before it fires.
739: Built around Skorpekh Lords leading Skorpekh Destroyers and Ophydian Destroyers, Canoptek Wraiths screening for C'tan Shards of the Void Dragon and the Nightbringer, and Illuminor Szeras and Technomancers keeping bodies on the table through Canoptek Reanimators, Awakened Dynasty is a melee-heavy threat-multiplier army. The engine is the detachment's +1 to Hit on Character-led units: Skorpekh Lords push Destroyers and Ophydians into elite close-combat reliability, while the C'tan punch through armour independently, forcing opponents to split resources across too many dangerous vectors to contain cleanly. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that cannot reposition fast enough to avoid being engulfed by Ophydians deep-striking into flanks while Wraiths lock down screens. Against fast alpha-strike armies or high-volume mortal-wound output that bypass Reanimation before the Technomancers can act, the recovery engine collapses and the melee threat packages arrive piecemeal rather than simultaneously.
767: Built around Boyz mobs, Gretchin screens, Painboys, Ghazghkull Thraka, Warboss, Wazdakka Gutsmek, Kommandos, Zodgrod Wortsnagga, and Flash Gitz, this is a Equatorial Hordes and Freebooter Krew double-detachment horde that drowns the board in Orks Infantry bodies while generating Sustained Hits 1 on virtually every attack across the entire force. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that can't realistically kill through the wave fast enough to deny objectives before the Orks lock in mid-table control. Blast-heavy, high-damage-per-shot lists that can delete entire Boyz mobs in one activation crack it open by outpacing the Painboys' ability to keep the horde alive.
557: Built around Beast Snagga Boyz, Beastboss characters, Squighog Boyz, Boyz, Gretchin screens, Kill Rig, Ghazghkull Thraka, Mozrog Skragbad, Painboy support, and Kommandos, this is a thundering green tide that floods the midboard with expendable bodies and hard-hitting Beast Snagga units. It punishes elite low-model armies badly — those opponents simply cannot kill enough models fast enough to deny board control before the Orks crush them in melee. Tightly packed, high-damage shooting armies that can thin the horde before contact, combined with anti-horde area denial, are the primary threat, as losing model count early collapses the combat weight the list depends on.
683: Built around Intercessor Squads, Heavy Intercessors, Assault Intercessors, and Librarians, this is a Bastion Task Force gunline that floods the board with Adeptus Astartes Battleline infantry — units that can shoot, charge, and perform Actions even after Advancing or Falling Back, collapsing the usual trade-off between mobility and firepower. The win condition is sustained board presence: Battleline units hit enemies and apply a debuff after each attack sequence, while Librarians cycle Psychic Disciplines each round — Divination for re-rolls when grinding, Biomancy for extra movement to contest objectives. It punishes elite low-model-count armies that cannot match the volume of bodies, forcing opponents into unfavourable trades against durable Heavy Intercessors anchoring midfield. Fast melee or alpha-strike lists that can isolate and delete squads in detail before the Battleline synergies engage will crack it open.
554: Built around Aethon Shaan, Kayvaan Shrike, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Vanguard Veterans with Jump Packs, Inceptors, and a screen of Scouts, Incursors, and Infiltrators backed by Centurion Devastators, this is a Shadowmark Talon force that blends a persistent ranged defence with aggressive jump-pack pressure. 760: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators, Logan Grimnar, Terminator Assault Squad, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and Arjac Rockfist, this is a transport-heavy terminator hammer that floods the mid-table with armoured bodies. 759: Built around Logan Grimnar, multiple squads of Wolf Guard Terminators, Arjac Rockfist, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, and a Captain in Terminator Armour, this is a Saga of the Great Wolf list that floods the board with elite, heavily armoured infantry. It struggles against extreme-range gunlines and armies that can strip wounds efficiently from a distance before the blobs ever make contact.
773: Built around Tzaangor Enlightened screening a tight castle of Sorcerers, Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Rubric Marines, and Scarab Occult Terminators, this list stacks Psyker synergies to sustain its own durability — most lists run Ritual of Regeneration, healing Psyker infantry each turn they manifest a Ritual. The win condition is attrition: heal faster than the opponent can kill, hold mid-board objectives behind layered invulnerable saves and replenished wounds, while Scarab Occult and Rubrics grind out mortal wounds at range. It punishes slow, low-volume-fire armies that cannot overload its regeneration loop and invulnerables before the scoring clock runs out. It cracks open against high-output shooting or alpha-strike lists that can delete entire units before healing triggers, bypassing the castle entirely.
771: Built around Sorcerers in Terminator Armour leading Scarab Occult Terminators, massed Sekhetar Robots, Rubric Marines as a midfield body, and Tzaangor chaff screens backed by Fatecaster Enlightened, this list layers a dense horde of durable infantry across every tier of the board. The win condition is attrition through volume — Psyker-adjacent Sekhetar Robots gaining +1 WS and Psychic attacks grind melee while Fatecaster bows and Rubric guns pressure mid-range objectives, letting the army score through sheer presence and staying power. It cracks under concentrated anti-infantry volume fire or alpha-strike threat saturation, since losing the Tzaangor screens early exposes the expensive core to focused removal before they can trade efficiently.
772: Built around Magnus the Red, Tzaangor Enlightened, Rubric Marines, Sorcerors, a winged Daemon Prince, Scarab Occult Terminators, Chaos Spawn, Sekhetar Robots, and Tzaangors under the Grand Coven detachment, this is a layered psychic army that floods the board with bodies while projecting serious ranged threat. 774: Built around Defilers, Forgefiends, Sekhetar Robots, a winged Daemon Prince, Tzaangor Enlightened with Fatecaster Greatbows, and half the time Magnus the Red, this is a Hexwarp Thrallband list that floods the board with Daemon Engines and Psychic-tagged melee threats. 780: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Sorcerers, and Chaos Spawn screening in mass numbers, this Grand Coven list uses the detachment's rotating Command phase abilities — including extended Psychic weapon range and enhanced Psychic shooting — to project overwhelming firepower while flooding the board with bodies. The win condition is layering Psychic shooting from Magnus and Rubric Marines behind a thick Chaos Spawn and Tzaangor screen, using mobile pieces like the winged Daemon Prince and Exalted Sorcerer on Disc to threaten flanks and pressure secondaries. It punishes static gunlines that struggle to chew through horde bodies before the Psychic payoff units get range-extended and into position. It cracks open against elite melee armies that can punch through the screen cleanly and close into Magnus before the Psychic abilities cycle through their one-per-battle uses.
611: Built around Khorne Berzerkers, Exalted Eightbound, Eightbound, Slaughterbound, and Angron, all delivered under the Berzerker Warband detachment's charge bonus — +1 Attack and +2 Strength on every melee weapon the moment they hit combat — with Jakhals, Chaos Spawn, and Chaos Rhinos providing screens, bodies, and transport efficiency. It cracks against gunlines and alpha-strike lists that strip the charge bonus by killing key units in movement or blocking charges with dense screens before the wave lands.
792: Built around Corsair Voidscarred, Prince Yriel, Corsair Voidreavers, Corsair Skyreavers, Warp Spiders, Striking Scorpions, Lhykhis, Rangers, Shroud Runners, and the Avatar of Khaine, this Eldritch Raiders list weaponizes the detachment's core rule — Anhrathe, Rangers, and Shroud Runners units can Advance and still charge — to flood the board with fast, multi-layered lethal threats from turn one. 789: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs led by Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and a supporting core of Assault Intercessors and Bladeguard Veterans, this list runs primarily under the Liberator Assault Group detachment, which adds 2 Strength and 1 Attack to all melee weapons on any unit that charged that turn. 788: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Commander Dante, Death Company Marines with jump packs, and a dense support stack of jump-pack Captains, Chaplains, and Vanguard Veterans, this list runs almost entirely airborne infantry under the Stormlance Task Force, with Vengeful Hosts providing hit-reroll support after ingress or charge moves. 648: Built around Huron Blackheart, Chosen, Warp Talons, Defilers, and swarms of Cultists and Red Corsairs Raiders, this Murdertalon Raiders and Veterans Of The Long War list plays a layered, high-mobility horde that punches well above its body count. 785: Built around Rotigus, Deathshroud Terminators, a Lord of Contagion, and waves of Beasts of Nurgle, Nurglings, Poxwalkers, Plaguebearers, and Chaos Spawn, this Tallyband Summoners list exploits the detachment's core synergy: Plague Legions daemons sitting within 7" of Death Guard units gain Nurgle's Gift, while Death Guard within 7" of those daemons extend their Contagion Range by 3", creating an interlocking web of attrition across the entire midboard. 782: Built around Mortarion, Deathshroud Terminators, a Daemon Prince of Nurgle, Foetid Bloat-Drones, and a deep roster of supporting characters running Virulent Vectorium, this list plants Poxwalkers and Chaos Spawn on objectives to trigger the detachment's Afflicted condition while a slow-rolling wall of elite infantry and Defilers grinds forward. 768: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beastboss on Squigosaur, Ghazghkull Thraka, Beast Snagga Boyz, and Boyz packed into Trukks, this is a Freebooter Krew horde that plays as a relentless mid-board brawler — designating a loot objective each Command phase to funnel pressure onto a single priority marker while the mass of bodies contests everywhere else. 794: Built around Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Arjac Rockfist, Wolf Guard Terminators, Wolf Guard Headtakers, and Vindicators operating under the Saga of the Great Wolf detachment, this list blends armoured firepower with elite melee infantry. 696: Built around Wolf Guard Terminators in multiple squads, Logan Grimnar, Bjorn the Fell-Handed, Wolf Guard Headtakers, Arjac Rockfist, Ragnar Blackmane, Wolf Guard Battle Leaders, Wulfen with Storm Shields, Blood Claws, and Intercessors, this is a melee-heavy Terminator tide that leverages the Saga Of The Beastslayer detachment's Lethal Hits on every attack targeting Characters, Monsters, and Vehicles. 776: Built around Magnus the Red, Rubric Marines, Scarab Occult Terminators, Tzaangor Enlightened with fatecaster greatbows, Sekhetar Robots, and a deep Sorcerer support stack, Grand Coven floods the board with layered psychic lethality across multiple unit types and ranges. 871: Built around Celestian Sacresants, Hospitaller support, Immolators, Paragon Warsuits, Seraphim, Zephyrim, and a dense command structure of Morvenn Vahl, Canonesses, and Junith Eruita, this is a mobile infantry swarm that floods the board from transports and the air. 718: Built around Immolators, Castigators, Dominion Squads, Paragon Warsuits, Morvenn Vahl, Celestian Sacresants, and Battle Sisters, this is a mechanised fire-army that turns every Adepta Sororitas ranged weapon into an Assault weapon and adds +1 Strength against anything within 6", rewarding relentless close-range aggression. 438: Built around Kastelan Robots paired with Cybernetica Datasmiths, Belisarius Cawl, Onager Dunecrawlers, and dense bodies of Skitarii Rangers, Vanguard, and Sicarian Infiltrators, this list runs the Lords Of The Forge detachment, granting Tech-Priest models a 4+ invulnerable save and Feel No Pain 5+ alongside the Baffling Data Screed debuff that hammers enemy vehicles at close range. 632: Built around Belisarius Cawl, Thulia Ghuld, dense Sicarian Ruststalker and Infiltrator blobs, Pteraxii Skystalkers, Ironstrider Ballistarii, and Servitor Battleclades, this is a transported infantry swarm that floods the mid-table with layered, lethal close-combat pressure. 499: Built around Morvenn Vahl, Paragon Warsuits, Castigators, and a deep bench of Immolators shuttling Canonesses, Zephyrim, Seraphim, and Dominion squads, this Army Of Faith list leans hard into mobile firepower across every range band. It cracks under pressure from fast alpha-strike armies that can isolate and delete Vahl or the Sacresant blobs before Hospitaller healing compounds, collapsing the board-hold engine.

656: Built around Prince Yriel, Lhykhis, the Avatar of Khaine, and deep waves of Corsair Skyreavers, Voidreavers, and Voidscarred, backed by Rangers, Shroud Runners, Warp Spiders, Howling Banshees, and Fire Prisms, this is a high-volume Aeldari horde that floods the table with cheap, mobile bodies layered over elite threat pieces. 576: Built around a full suite of Aspect Warriors — Howling Banshees led by Jain Zar and Lhykhis, Warp Spiders, Swooping Hawks, Fire Dragons, Striking Scorpions, Dark Reapers, and Dire Avengers anchored by Asurmen and the Avatar of Khaine — this is a layered, all-Aspect list running the Aspect Host detachment, which grants every Aspect unit a re-roll of 1s to hit or wound each time it shoots or fights.
