655: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Farseers, Warlock Skyrunners, War Walkers, and Storm Guardians flooding the board under the Armoured Warhost detachment — with Seer Council's Fate dice pool giving the psyker spine reliable Stratagem fuel from turn one. The engine is layered lethality: War Walkers advance-and-fire freely via the Assault rule on vehicle ranged attacks, while the dense psyker stack buffs, protects, and repositions infantry screens to contest every objective and drain opponent CP through attrition. It punishes low-model-count elite lists that struggle to clear multiple overlapping screens and absorb the volume of mobile anti-armour the War Walkers and vehicle core generate across every game phase. It cracks under pressure from high-AP alpha strikes that can collapse the screening infantry before the Fate dice pool pays off, leaving the psyker characters dangerously exposed.
813: Built around Windriders, Shining Spears, Warlock Skyrunners, Farseer Skyrunners, Rangers, Fire Dragons, War Walkers, and Howling Banshees, this is a fast, layered Aeldari force that floods the board with Mounted keyword units the Windrider Host detachment can deploy from Strategic Reserves at accelerated timing, keeping them safe until the moment they strike. The win condition is attrition through positioning — cycling skimmers onto objectives while Shining Spears and Fire Dragons peel armour and Howling Banshees threaten elite infantry in melee, with Eldrad Ulthran and Farseer Skyrunners stacking support to maximise damage output each phase. It punishes slow, static lists that cannot contest multiple flanks simultaneously, as the reserve-entry trick lets Mounted units appear where screens are thinnest. Armies with reliable long-range anti-skimmer volume or aggressive deep-strike pressure can collapse its tempo before the reserves arrive to answer.
810: Built around Troupes embarked in Starweavers, Troupe Masters, Solitaires, Skyweavers, and Rangers, this is a mobile Harlequins-heavy infantry force that blends transport-delivered melee threats with skimmer fire support. The core engine is disembarkation: Troupes pile out of Starweavers mid-board, triggering Sustained Hits 1 on their weapons via Serpent's Brood, then crash into priority targets while Starweavers and Skyweavers pour Assault-tagged fire from Armoured Warhost into anything still standing. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that cannot screen effectively, as layered Sustained Hits volume shreds them before they can consolidate. However, it cracks against armies that can shut down the transport delivery system early — killing Starweavers before disembarkation collapses the kill chain entirely, and at 40% wins this strategy is clearly struggling to survive that pressure.
809: Built around Eldrad Ulthran, multiple Warlock Conclaves, Farseers, Warlock Skyrunners, War Walkers, Storm Guardians, and Rangers, this is a layered psychic-support army running primarily Seer Council, generating a pool of Fate dice at the start of the game to fuel detachment Stratagems throughout the match. The plan is to saturate the board with cheap, hard-to-kill screening bodies while War Walkers and mobile psyker units pour layered lethal fire into anything that contests objectives, using the Fate dice engine to spike critical Stratagem activations at the right moment. It punishes slow, low-model-count armies that can't clear screens efficiently, as the sheer volume of bodies forces opponents into unfavorable trades while psychic-buffed shooting picks apart exposed key pieces. It cracks under sustained alpha-strike pressure or armies that delete screening units cheaply in bulk, collapsing the layered defensive structure before the Fate dice engine can pay off.
577: Built around Windriders, Warlock Skyrunners, Shroud Runners, Rangers, War Walkers, Shining Spears, Warp Spiders, Eldrad Ulthran, Lhykhis, and Farseer Skyrunners, this is a mobile, layered shooting force that floods the board with fast skimmer platforms and uses the Path Of The Outcast detachment to extend detection range on Ranger and Shroud Runner activations, stripping cover and exposing targets for follow-up fire. The Windrider Host pulls most mounted units off the table at deployment then redeploys them a round early, engineering favorable angles to chain lethal fire into priority targets while Rangers and Shroud Runners pin down infiltrators and deny forward positions. It punishes slow or static armies that rely on cover and positioning, as the detection mechanic and sheer volume of layered shooting across multiple activations dismantles those defensive setups. It struggles against aggressive alpha-strike lists that can close range before the reserve engine resolves, or heavy armored threats that survive the initial volleys and collapse the light skimmer bodies in return.
585: Built around Bullgryn Squads, Commissars, Tech-Priest Enginseers, and Hellhounds, this list uses the Abhuman Auxiliaries detachment to enable Commissars to issue Orders directly to Bullgryns, keeping the big brutes hitting hard while Enginseers maintain vehicles and Hellhounds threaten flanks. The plan is to anchor the midfield with Bullgryns absorbing pressure while a heavy gunline — anchored on large armoured pieces under Steel Hammer — punishes anything that tries to clear them, shooting into engagements without penalty. It punishes slower, attrition-based armies that want to trade efficiently at range, because the Bullgryn wall forces unfavorable melee engagements while the armour farm grinds from behind. It cracks against elite fast armies that can isolate and overwhelm individual Bullgryn blocks before the gunline repositions, exploiting the list's limited board-wide mobility.
856: Built around Wraithguard, Wraithblades, Wraithlords, Spiritseers, Warlock Skyrunners, and Fire Prisms, this list runs Armoured Warhost alongside Spirit Conclave to create a self-reinforcing kill engine: every Spiritseer the opponent destroys loads Vengeful Dead tokens onto the killing unit, and every subsequent Wraith Construct attack against that unit hits and wounds on improved rolls. The plan is to bait enemy fire into the Psyker screen, then avalanche boosted Wraith Construct attacks — backed by Assault-enabled Fire Prism shooting on the move — into whatever overextended to take the bait. It punishes slower gunlines that must commit resources to remove the Psyker bubble, triggering the revenge loop repeatedly while mobile Warlock Skyrunners contest objectives. Aggressive alpha-strike lists that can delete both the Psyker enablers and the Wraith Constructs simultaneously before tokens accumulate crack this open before the engine ever fires.
811: Built around Wraithlords, Wraithguard, Wraithblades, Spiritseers, and Warlock Skyrunners, this Spirit Conclave list weaponizes its own psyker deaths as a kill engine — every Asuryani Psyker the opponent destroys loads Vengeful Dead tokens onto their unit, and every subsequent Wraith Construct attack into that unit hits and wounds on improved rolls. The plan is to bait early psyker casualties, then avalanche buffed Wraith Construct melee and shooting into token-loaded targets to snowball lethal pressure across mid-table objectives. Mobile Warlock and Farseer Skyrunners keep the aura network intact while Wraithguard provide layered anti-armour overload that punishes static gunlines unable to spread their fire efficiently. The build cracks when opponents ignore the psykers entirely or out-range the short-threat Wraith infantry before tokens ever accumulate.
818: Built around the Baneblade, Tech-Priest Enginseers, Lord Solar Leontus, Cadian Shock Troops, and Hellhounds, this Steel Hammer gunline plants its superheavies at range and uses Enginseers to keep them fighting, while Hellhounds and infantry hold mid-table presence. The plan is to leverage Steel Hammer's ability to fire freely even into engagement range — letting Titanic and Squadron units blast anything that dares close in — while Lord Solar drives tempo and Shock Troops screen objectives. It punishes slow, durable armies that can't threaten multiple superheavies simultaneously, grinding them down under sustained heavy firepower before they can trade efficiently. Fast, high-volume deep-striking assault lists or anything that can isolate and overwhelm a single Baneblade in melee will crack it open, as losing even one Titanic unit dramatically collapses the damage output.
663: Built around Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Exterminators, Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Scout Sentinels, Cadian Shock Troops, Cadian Command Squads, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this is a heavy armoured gunline that floods the board with high-volume, long-range firepower. Combined Arms' Lethal Hits on Squadron units against Monsters and Vehicles is the engine — tank after tank cycling fire through command-squad Orders to grind opposing armour and monsters off the table while infantry screens hold objectives and Scout Sentinels create forward pressure. It punishes elite vehicle-heavy lists that cannot close the distance fast enough, letting Lethal Hits convert weight of shots into consistent damage before the opponent can answer. Armies that can alpha-strike the tank line directly, deny line of sight, or flood the board with cheap bodies to absorb shots and contest objectives will crack it open before the firepower pays off.
547: Built around Tech-Priest Enginseers, Scout Sentinels, Lord Solar Leontus, a Banesword, a Baneblade, and Gaunt's Ghosts, this list uses the Designation Force detachment to give Sentinels and Infantry units the Signal Flares ability, then layers Steel Hammer on top so its Titanic and Squadron units can fire point-blank into engaged enemies without penalty. The plan is to park superheavies in a defensive gunline, use Signal Flares to light up priority targets, and delete them with massed Titanic firepower while Gaunt's Ghosts and Leontus hold or contest objectives. It punishes elite, low-model-count armies that struggle to close distance before the superheavies strip their key pieces off the board. Any list that can alpha-strike a superheavy or two early, or flood the mid-board with durable screening bodies to deny firing lanes, will crack this build open before the gunline pays for itself.
548: Built around Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Leman Russ Exterminators, Rogal Dorn Commanders, and Hellhounds, with Tempestus Scions, Tempestus Aquilons, Scout Sentinels, and Cadian Shock Troops rounding out the force under Bridgehead Strike. The plan is to flood the board with armour and drop Scions mid-game with +1 to hit on arrival, using Combined Arms' Lethal Hits on Squadron units to crack opposing vehicles while the Russ gunline and Hellhounds grind anything that contests objectives. It punishes elite-light armies that lack anti-tank overload by drowning them in durable vehicles that require more firepower to remove than they typically carry. It cracks open against high-volume anti-tank spam or alpha-strike lists that can strip the armoured core before the Scions' drop amplifies output enough to matter.
837: Built around Marshal, Castellan, and High Marshal Helbrecht leading Sword Brethren and Crusader squads alongside a core of Repulsor Executioners, with the Emperor's Champion as a melee hammer, this is a hybrid gunline-assault force spread across three detachments — most commonly The Living Miracle, granting the Champion re-rolls on hit and wound in melee. The plan is to park Repulsor Executioners as a skimmer fire platform while character-buffed infantry blobs contest objectives and the Emperor's Champion punishes anything that steps into melee range. It excels against mid-density infantry armies that can't efficiently trade into both the heavy vehicle shooting and the close-combat threat simultaneously. It struggles against lists that can strip the Repulsor Executioners early through anti-tank overload, leaving the infantry core without enough firepower to close out games.
583: Built around Kasrkin, Cadian Shock Troops, and Chimeras supported by a dense officer corps of Cadian Castellans and Command Squads, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with Orders-buffed infantry firing from transports and dug-in positions, with Bullgryns providing a close-range anvil and Tech-Priest Enginseers keeping vehicles in the fight. The win condition is volume attrition — Officers stack Orders to trigger re-rolls on hit rolls of 1 across multiple units simultaneously, letting Kasrkin and Shock Troops punch well above their points while Chimeras project threat across mid-board objectives. It punishes horde and medium-infantry lists badly, overwhelming them with mass re-rolled fire before they can trade efficiently. However, elite low-model-count armies that can isolate and delete the officer bubble or hard-target the lightly armoured Chimeras will collapse the Order chain and gut the build's output.
819: Built around Rogal Dorn Commanders, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Battle Tanks, Gaunt's Ghosts, Bullgryns, and Lord Solar Leontus operating under Grizzled Company, this is a mechanised gunline that floods the table with armour, elite infantry screens, and officer-stacked Orders that let every attacking model re-roll hit rolls of 1 while increasing the number of Orders each officer can issue. The win condition is layered attrition: Rogal Dorn Commanders and Leman Russ tanks grind through armour at range while Hellhounds flush out light infantry and Bullgryns bodyblock key pieces long enough for the gunline to dismantle threats systematically. It punishes slow, static enemy lists that cannot close distance quickly, as sustained heavy firepower with consistent hit re-rolls overwhelms low-mobility armies before they establish board presence. The list cracks under pressure from fast melee or alpha-strike builds that can punch through the infantry screens early, exposing the armour to close-range engagements where the gunline's range advantage collapses.
817: Built around Hellhounds, a Doomhammer, Scout Sentinels, Bullgryns, and Tech-Priest Enginseers supported by Lord Solar Leontus and Cadian Command Squads, this list runs Abhuman Auxiliaries and Steel Hammer to combine a mobile armoured fist with a grinding super-heavy gunline. The win condition is pushing Hellhounds and Bullgryns aggressively into midboard to contest objectives while the Doomhammer — benefiting from Steel Hammer's ability to fire into engagements without penalty — hammers anything that tries to screen or tie it up, with Enginseers keeping the vehicle core repaired and operational throughout. It punishes elite melee threats and mid-density infantry screens hard, as Bullgryns absorb punishment on the push while the Squadron rule lets titanic firepower fire freely through the scrum. Highly mobile, high-damage lists that can alpha strike the Hellhounds off the board or deny the Doomhammer clear lanes will crack it open, since losing either the mobile vanguard or the super-heavy anchor collapses the two-layer pressure the build depends on.
661: Built around Tempestus Scions, Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Cadian Shock Troops, Kasrkin, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Rogal Dorn Commanders, all ferried and supported by Tauroxes, with Gaunt's Ghosts providing elite infiltration muscle — this is a deep-order, mass-infantry gunline running Grizzled Company, which boosts Officer Order capacity and grants re-rolls of 1 to hit on all affected units. The plan is to stack multiple Orders across a wide infantry line, activate the re-roll engine on as many squads as possible simultaneously, and grind the opponent off objectives through sheer volume of accurate, mobile anti-armour and skimmer fire. It punishes armies that rely on durable mid-table units — the combination of Taurox mobility, Scion deep strikes, and Rogal Dorn firepower creates overlapping kill lanes that few medium-durability targets survive. It cracks under pressure from elite alpha-strike lists that can surgically remove Officers before Orders resolve, collapsing the re-roll engine and leaving a fragile horde with no damage amplification.
475: Built around dense Battleline infantry — Crusader Squads, Assault Intercessors, and Intercessors backed by Scout Squads and Sword Brethren — sitting behind a core of Repulsor Executioners, with the Emperor's Champion, Marshal, and Castellan providing character support throughout. The engine is the Bastion Task Force's Battleline rule: units that Advance or Fall Back remain eligible to shoot, charge, and perform Actions, letting infantry hold and score objectives while Repulsor Executioners deliver sustained heavy fire from elevated or protected positions. This setup punishes slow midfield armies and infantry-heavy hordes, using mass bodies to contest every corner while the Executioners apply relentless anti-tank overload from range. It struggles against fast, high-damage opponents who can crack the Executioners early and collapse the infantry screen before the Action economy generates enough points.
864: Built around Crusader Squads, Sword Brethren, the Emperor's Champion, Execrators, Repulsor Executioners, and High Marshal Helbrecht, this is a Companions of Vehemence gunline that pairs massed infantry bodies with heavy skimmer firepower — advancing and charging freely thanks to the detachment's universal re-roll on both Advance and Charge rolls, collapsing the gap between shooting and melee phases. The plan is to flood midboard with cheap scoring chaff while Repulsor Executioners pour layered fire into dense targets, then convert the advance-and-charge re-rolls into contested objective fights that bleed opponents on secondaries. It punishes mass-horde and heavy gunline armies hardest, where its own volume of bodies and reliable threat-range on multiple units overwhelms slower positioning games. It cracks under elite, high-damage alpha strikes — the infantry core is fragile individually, and if the Execrators and Repulsors are stripped early, the charge engine stalls without the shooting buffer to protect it.
694: Built around Repulsor Executioners, Gladiator Lancers, and a dense support web of Techmarines, Castellans, and Marshals, with the Emperor's Champion and Sword Brethren providing a melee threat alongside the vehicle core, all running Ironstorm Spearhead for per-unit hit, wound, or damage re-rolls on every Adeptus Astartes unit each phase. The plan is to project overwhelming heavy firepower from durable skimmers while Sword Brethren and the Emperor's Champion — sharpened further in most lists by The Living Miracle's fight-phase re-rolls — contest mid-table and punish anything that tries to close the distance. This build hammers armoured lists hard, stacking mobile anti-tank volume across multiple vehicles with re-roll support that keeps damage output consistent even through partial hits. It struggles against fast armies that can swamp its infantry screens and tie up the vehicles in combat before the gunline can leverage its range.
836: Built around the Emperor's Champion, High Marshal Helbrecht, multiple Repulsor Executioners, Execrators, and dense infantry blocks of Sword Brethren, Crusader Squads, Assault Intercessors, Scouts, and Intercessors, this list plants itself inside terrain and grinds from fixed positions. The Ceramite Sentinels detachment rewards staying put — units inside terrain gain re-rolls to hit and wound rolls of 1, and earn the Entrenched keyword, turning every piece of cover into a fighting position while the Repulsor Executioners and Execrators pour skimmer fire downfield. It punishes armies that must advance into its kill zones, stacking re-roll efficiency against anything trying to dislodge entrenched infantry or trade into massed heavy vehicles. Highly mobile alpha-strike forces and deep-striking armies that land behind the gunline or force it off terrain before Entrenched activates will crack it open, since the entire engine collapses the moment units are displaced or set up mid-turn.
787: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs, Sanguinary Priests, Commander Dante, and Lemartes, this is a wall-to-wall jump infantry list running the Liberator Assault Group detachment, which grants +2 Strength and +1 Attack to all melee weapons on any unit that charged that turn. The plan is to flood multiple lanes simultaneously with buffed charging units, using Scouts and Intercessors to screen objectives while the jump pack elements crash into priority targets with inflated combat stats. It punishes combat-light lists and anything that relies on durable mid-range infantry, since the charge bonus converts even mid-tier melee units into serious threats across every fight phase simultaneously. However, it struggles against armies that can deny or redirect charges — anything with strong overwatch, tight screens, or ranged alpha-strike output can prevent the charge triggers entirely, stripping the build of its core damage engine.
446: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, Captains with Jump Packs, Lemartes, Sanguinary Priests, and Scout and Intercessor squads holding ground, Legacy of Grace pairs with Stormlance Task Force to create a jump infantry hammer that can Advance and still declare charges — with an additional +1 to both rolls from the detachment stacking directly onto that engine. The plan is to flood mid-table with screens while the jump pack core surges forward turn one, threatens charges off Advances, and deletes priority targets through sheer melee volume. It punishes slow, static gunlines that cannot reposition to avoid the inevitable charge threat from multiple angles simultaneously. It cracks open against elite melee armies or anything with reliable overwatch and dense screening that can absorb the alpha and fight back on even terms.
644: Built around multiple Sanguinary Guard squads, Captains with jump packs, Commander Dante, Death Company Marines, Assault Intercessors with jump packs, Chaplains, and Inceptors, this is an all-jump-pack assault force running the Encarmine Speartip detachment. The central engine is Sanguinary Guard cycling in and out of melee — falling back without losing eligibility to shoot or charge keeps them perpetually active, while Dante and Chaplains stack buffs to amplify elite kill output turn after turn. It punishes lower-model-count armies that can't hold every flank simultaneously, overwhelming them through multi-threat jump assaults that never fully disengage. It cracks against armies that can screen aggressively or deliver high-volume anti-elite shooting, since losing Sanguinary Guard bodies early collapses the entire kill chain.
669: Built around Be'lakor, one or two Lords of Change, a Bloodthirster, and screening bodies in Plaguebearers, Flesh Hounds, Screamers, and Cultist Mobs, this is a Shadow Legion force that weaponises layered threat across every phase. The win condition is forcing opponents into impossible priority choices — Be'lakor's Shadow Legion abilities (often enhanced by Fade to Darkness) enable aggressive repositioning while the Bloodthirster and Lords of Change deliver multi-vector lethal pressure from different angles. Warptide, taken in three-quarters of lists, allows Battleline units to advance and still charge, turning screens into genuine threats and punishing static gunlines that rely on maintaining safe firing lanes. However, the build's relatively low model density and reliance on individual character-sized pieces means concentrated high-volume firepower or efficient anti-large shooting can strip key threats faster than the list can recover.
671:
Built around Flesh Hounds as the primary engine, this is a red tide of Khorne daemon infantry and cavalry flooding the midboard through Warptide's advance-and-charge permission and Blood Legion's reactive surge moves that punish enemies for simply moving near your units.

The plan is to use Warptide to advance battleline units without losing charge eligibility, then trigger Blood Legion surges in the opponent's movement phase to close gaps and pile into combat from unexpected angles, generating a layered threat chain across multiple activations.

It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility armies that cannot avoid entering the 8" Blood Legion trigger zone, where reactive surges compound into devastating multi-unit pile-ins before the opponent can disengage.

It cracks when faced with high-mobility armies that can consistently stay outside 8", or elite melee threats that can isolate and delete each wave in detail before the numbers compound.
670: Built around Flesh Hounds, Be'lakor, Skarbrand, a Lord of Change, a Great Unclean One, and Beasts of Nurgle, this is a mobile, multi-threat daemon swarm using the Daemonic Incursion detachment to drop reinforcements directly into the fight — threatening to land units safely near friendly Greater Daemons or inside the Shadow of Chaos rather than scattering into the open. The win condition is threat saturation: Skarbrand and Bloodthirsters punch through elite infantry while screamers and Flesh Hounds contest and flip objectives across the board, forcing opponents to split attention across multiple lethal vectors simultaneously. It punishes static, low-mobility armies that can't reposition to address deep-striking threats arriving from multiple angles each turn. Its weakness is volume shooting and elite gunlines that can isolate and delete individual Greater Daemons before the threat web assembles, collapsing the layered lethality that makes the engine work.
748: Built around a mixed War Dog pack of Executioners, Karnivores, Stalkers, and Brigands supported by a Knight Abominant and Knight Ruinator, the Helhunt Lance runs under its eponymous detachment, which feeds the Titanic Knights' own Aura buffs back onto themselves whenever two or more War Dogs are in range — turning every support bubble into a self-amplifying kill engine. The plan is to flood mid-board with layered lethality, using the Abominant's aura to supercharge the pack while the Ruinator and War Dogs strip armour at every range band simultaneously. It punishes elite vehicle-heavy lists that can't clear wounds fast enough, as the sheer volume of mobile anti-armour across multiple Titanic and War Dog bodies forces impossible priority decisions. Tight infantry screens and high-volume mortal-wound output crack it open by choking movement lanes and grinding the War Dogs before the aura synergies can compound.
687: Built around War Dog Executioners, War Dog Brigands, War Dog Karnivores, a Knight Abominant, and a Knight Rampager, this is a fast, all-armour swarm that layers War Dogs and big Knights across every angle of the board. The Hunting Warpack's detection mechanic strips Lone Operative and hidden-unit protections off enemy screens, while Traitoris Lance lets the army hand-pick an additional Dread ability at game start, stacking threat profiles before a shot is fired. It punishes transport-heavy and armoured lists through sheer anti-armour volume and layered lethal output that overwhelms damage-mitigation sequences. It cracks when faced with durable elite infantry or armies that can kite and zone it off objectives, since the list has no cheap bodies to contest and bleeds points when its Knights can't reach their targets.
651: Built around Cultist Mobs screening objectives, Legionaries and Chosen piling out of Chaos Rhinos into midfield brawls, and a Chaos Lord driving the close-range threat package, this is a mechanically diverse infantry-and-transport force with no single dominant detachment anchoring its identity. The plan is to flood the midboard with bodies — Cultists absorbing pressure while Rhino-borne Chosen and Legionaries deliver melee payloads into scoring positions, supported by heavy gunline elements blanketing the table. It punishes slower midrange armies that can't clear chaff efficiently, exploiting the sheer volume of threats arriving simultaneously from transports and foot screens. However, elite shooting lists that strip Rhinos early and collapse the screen deny the delivery mechanism entirely, leaving the melee payload stranded and the objective game gutted.
590: Built around the Knight Tyrant and Knight Despoiler, this is a towering wall of Chaos war engines that leverages the Bastions Of Tyranny detachment's core mechanic: once enemies are battle-shocked, the Tyrant's attacks gain +1 to hit, creating a brutal feedback loop where disruption accelerates annihilation. The plan is to overwhelm opposing armour with layered anti-tank firepower across multiple threat vectors simultaneously, forcing impossible target-priority decisions while chipping battle-shock to unlock the hit-roll bonus. It punishes elite vehicle-heavy lists that cannot spread their defensive resources thin enough to contain multiple Knight-scale threats advancing in parallel. The weakness is anything that avoids battle-shock reliably or applies sufficient mortal wounds at range to crack the biggest pieces before the Tyrant can capitalise on disrupted enemies.
808: Built around double Forgefiends, Defilers, Warpsmiths, and Cultist Mob screens, this is a Daemon Engine gunline that leans on Dark Pact-fueled shooting to grind opponents off the board from range. The core engine is the Soulforged Warpack contract: Forgefiends and Defilers invoke their pact to add 1 to Wound rolls on ranged attacks, while Warpsmiths keep the machines operational and Cultists absorb punishment on forward objectives. It punishes low-armour, infantry-heavy armies that have to advance into its kill zones, where stacked Wound bonuses and volume of fire become overwhelming. Against elite melee armies that can close distance fast and tank the shooting phase, the build struggles — its Dark Pact Leadership risk and limited melee threat leave it exposed once engines are locked in combat.
820: Built around waves of Plaguebearers, Nurglings, Beasts of Nurgle, and Great Unclean Ones anchored by Rotigus and Poxbringer support, this is a slow-grinding Nurgle tide running Lords Of The Warp as its foundation and Plague Legion in nearly three-quarters of lists. The plan is to flood midfield with durable, Lethal-stacked bodies, forcing enemy units into the Plague Legion's Shadow of Chaos aura and bleeding them through mandatory Battle-shock tests each Command phase while Beasts of Nurgle and Great Unclean Ones brawl for primary objectives. It punishes low-leadership, attrition-resistant builds that expect to trade efficiently, as the layered durability and persistent Battle-shock pressure make unfavorable engagements increasingly costly over turns. However, it cracks against fast alpha-strike armies that can isolate and delete the Great Unclean Ones before the Nurgle bubble establishes itself, dismantling the Shadow of Chaos engine before it generates meaningful pressure.
449: Built around Chaos Terminator squads, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, and Cultist Mobs screening them forward, this is a grinding mid-board brawler that wins through attrition and presence rather than finesse. The plan is to plant Terminators and Mutilators on centrally contested objectives while Legionaries and Cultists absorb chip damage and trade up, letting the armoured core outlast opposing infantry across turns. It punishes elite low-model-count lists hard, where durable multi-wound units can absorb the firepower that would clear a horde while the screens deny easy charges. It cracks under concentrated high-AP anti-tank overload or heavy mortal wound output that bypasses the wound-roll resilience of the brick and strips both the screen and the expensive core in the same turn.
852: Built around Obliterators, Kravek Morne, Mutilators, Chaos Terminators, and Cultist Mobs supported by Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, this list runs Devotees of Destruction — granting Obliterators and Havocs [HEAVY] on all ranged attacks — and frequently pairs it with Warpstrike Champions, which lets up to two Terminator, Obliterator, or Mutilator units redeploy at the end of each opponent's turn. The plan is to flood the mid-board with cheap Cultist screens while cycling the heavy hitters into ideal threat positions every turn, using the Warpstrike repositioning engine to punish any defensive adjustment the opponent makes. It brutalises gunlines and static armour lists that can't relocate fast enough to escape a Mutilator or Terminator unit teleporting into their face. It struggles against fast, aggressive armies that can collapse the Cultist screens early and pin the expensive melee units in Engagement Range before the repositioning trigger fires.
728: Built around Chaos Terminators led by Sorcerers and Kravek Morne, backed by Mutilators and jump-pack infantry in Raptors and Warp Talons, this list layers two detachments: Murdertalon Raiders grants its FLY infantry re-rolls against weakened or battle-shocked targets and forces those same enemies to hit them at -1, while Warpstrike Champions redeploys up to two Terminator, Obliterator, or Mutilator units at the end of every opponent's turn, creating a relentless repositioning threat. The plan is to brawl through the mid-table, grind units below half-strength to trigger both halves of the Raiders ability, then teleport heavy hitters back into optimal positions to punish anything that tries to recover. It dismantles slow, durable gunlines by making Mutilators and Terminators almost impossible to efficiently remove when the attrition engine is running. Highly mobile elite armies that apply simultaneous pressure across multiple threat vectors can outpace the repositioning cadence and bypass the conditional defensive bonuses before battle-shock or casualty thresholds are reached.
650: Built around Cultist Mobs, Legionaries, Chosen, Chaos Rhinos, Sorcerers, Warpsmiths, and Chaos Lords, this is a layered mid-table infantry machine running Cabal of Chaos, boosting Psyker shooting through Dark Pact-powered Strength buffs while flooding the board with cheap bodies and elite footsloggers. The plan is to drown opponents in overlapping threat bubbles — screening with Cultists, pushing Legionaries and Chosen forward in Rhinos, and using Dark Pact synergies to punch above weight at range while contesting objectives through sheer volume. It punishes low-model-count elite armies that struggle to clear waves of Heretic Astartes infantry before the midgame objective race is already lost. Concentrated high-Strength shooting or combat lists that can systematically delete units faster than they score will crack it open, as the build lacks the durability to weather sustained anti-horde firepower across multiple turns.
524: Built around Azrael, Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, Lion El'Jonson, and Jump Pack Assault Intercessors screened by Scouts and Intercessors, this is a durable mid-board brawler running predominantly Wrath of the Rock, whose wound-roll subtraction on high-Strength attacks makes the melee core genuinely hard to remove through conventional anti-tank shooting. The plan is to park Azrael's aura onto the Deathwing Knights and Companions, grind through enemy units in combat while Intercessors and Scouts hold backfield objectives, and use Lion as a late-game hammer or counter-punch anchor. It punishes lists that rely on high-Strength, low-volume attacks to clear elite infantry, since that wound penalty bleeds efficiency exactly where those builds need it most. Armies that can flood mortal wounds, bring mass low-Strength volume, or out-range the melee core before it closes will crack it open, and the modest win rate suggests it struggles to close that gap consistently.
853: Built around Warp Talons, Venomcrawlers, Defilers, Vashtorr the Arkifane, and Warpsmith support, this is a daemon-engine-heavy force running Murdertalon Raiders as its primary detachment with Soulforged Warpack providing the offensive spike — when Daemon Vehicles invoke their Dark Pact contract, they gain +1 to wound on ranged attacks and +2 melee Attacks, turning already-dangerous machines into short-window wrecking balls. The plan is to pressure armour and mid-table objectives simultaneously, using Cultist Mobs to screen and hold while Venomcrawlers and Defilers punch through tanks and monsters with contract-fuelled kill chains. It punishes slow, low-model-count elite lists that struggle to screen out multiple daemon vehicles attacking from different angles.
